# Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized), Part II

This roadmap extends Tau Ceti's structural Hodge theory from individual fibres to connections, variations, period maps and their geometric and arithmetic applications. Its targets include complex non-abelian Hodge theory, canonical logarithmic extensions and fixed parts, parabolic rank bounds, rigidity and integrality, multivariable degeneration, algebraicity of Hodge loci and real Noether–Lefschetz cones. The existing pure and mixed Hodge structures, polarizations, opposed filtrations, Tate twists and period-domain points are the starting library. Their construction belongs to the original Hodge Structures roadmap.

The development has nine layers, H.0–H.8. Each layer specifies the objects it owns, the statements it needs, the API and tests of its definitions, and the exact dependency endpoints. A declaration is a planning target, with implementation status unchecked. All nine layers are planned with explicit gaps; none is closed. A prerequisite whose statement is itself conditional imports that conditional plan. Neither the dependency graph nor a well-typed suggested signature proves the mathematics or installs a supplier interface.

## Scope and ownership

H.0 owns Higgs and parameter-connection operators and the special algebra of their curvature, horizontal maps, ordered iteration, determinant, tensor operations and filtered symbols. H.1 owns operator stability and the complex moduli/correspondence applications. H.2 owns variation comparisons, canonical extensions, fixed parts and monodromy conclusions. H.3 owns general period-domain and period-derivative adapters. H.4 owns parabolic estimates and their unitary cohomological applications. H.5 owns rigidity, its Hodge consequences, arithmetic models and integrality. H.6 owns polarized degeneration and geometric logarithmic monodromy comparisons. H.7 owns the Hodge-specific use of tame arithmetic quotients and definable Chow. H.8 owns real variation and Noether–Lefschetz interfaces for its real-surface consumer.

## Conventions

Write O for the ring sheaf and Ω¹ for the supplied relative differential module. A relatively constant parameter λ satisfies dλ=0. A parameter connection is an additive operator D:E→E⊗Ω¹ with D(ae)=aD(e)+λe⊗da. Its exterior extension is D(e⊗ω)=D(e)∧ω+λe⊗dω, and integrability means its actual exterior curvature vanishes. At λ=0 this is a Higgs field; at λ=1 it is an ordinary connection. On a finite locally free chart D=λd+A. Twisted coefficients retain their invertible line and its action; a Tate frame is a choice, not a trivialization of the Galois character.

Ordered nilpotence uses the full tensor power of the coefficient module. The degree-zero iterate is the tensor-unit identity. Each successor inserts the newest coefficient in slot zero. Contracting a word gives an ordered product of endomorphisms, with the rightmost factor acting first. Integrability alone does not give ordered nilpotence. A global bound needs a common exponent; unbounded ranks on an infinite cover do not provide one. Kernels of iterates are subsheaves and need not be subbundles.

The finite Griffiths/Rees construction uses a decreasing bounded, locally split filtration with locally free graded pieces and ∇Fᵖ⊆Fᵖ⁻¹⊗Ω¹. Its Rees module is generated by t⁻ᵖFᵖ and has operator t∇. The zero, unit and inverted fibres retain their operator comparisons. Liu–Zhu's localized period lattice has an unbounded filtration and a Tate/Galois adapter of its own; it is not obtained by changing the name of a bounded Rees module.

A fixed determinant fixes its operator or character as well as its underlying line. On the projective H.1 component the prescribed determinant is torsion and rational Chern classes vanish. Stability is tested on invariant coherent subsheaves. Fixed-determinant deformation uses End₀, with determinant rigidification, residual scalar inertia and coarse invariant rings distinguished. A stable representation has positive rank. Stable coarse moduli need not be proper; the proper Hitchin target is the specified semistable one.

A complex polarized variation has a flat Hermitian polarization of the source's alternating sign on its Hodge pieces and need not carry a real form or lattice. A rational/integral variation includes that extra coefficient datum. The shared carrier belongs to D3. Canonical logarithmic extension chooses a residue strip; general tensor compatibility is not asserted without respecting that normalization. The unipotent branch has its own tensor comparison.

For a connection d+A dq/q and a positively oriented loop, T=exp(−2πiA). In degeneration write L=log T and use Φ(z)=exp(ΣzᵢLᵢ)Ψ(q), qᵢ=exp(2πizᵢ). The normalized logarithm Aᵢ=−Lᵢ/(2πi) is the residue convention. Sources using N for either operator are translated at their entries. Every multigrading σ in norm estimates is centered at zero; squared norms have exponent σ, whereas norms have exponent σ/2. The complex splitting I of Hodge and weight filtrations and the rational weight splitting J are distinct choices. Compact buffers and nondegenerating parameters remain in uniform statements.

General period domains and represented Mumford–Tate subdomains are distinct: a proper tensor-constrained orbit is not the full ambient domain. In arithmetic containment fix the canonical maximal compact K of the marked Hodge point. Schmid's one-variable torus need not be Cartan-stable for AA.3's convention; their comparison is an explicit supplier gap. H.7 proves algebraicity one special pullback at a time. Its exceptional Hodge locus is a countable union of algebraic subvarieties and is not asserted definable as a whole. Untwisted rational tensors have type (0,0); type (p,p) uses the Tate-twist adapter.

On a real weight-two variation distinguish the complex-linear geometric action σ_C, coefficient conjugation κ, and the conjugate-linear combined map σ_Cκ. Geometric action exchanges the Hodge indices; the combined map preserves type. The generator of Z(1) has real Galois sign −1, so the fixed subspace after twisting identifies with ker(σ+1). The moving-filtration period derivative is the connection symbol, while the obstruction derivative of a fixed flat class has its negative. The VHS lattice is integral cohomology modulo torsion; the ordinary integral topological theorems retain torsion.

## H.0 — Higgs and parameter connections

The algebra begins with commuting affine derivations and a relatively constant parameter. Coordinate curvature, gauge transport, tensor and dual operators provide concrete tests for the intrinsic sheaf definitions. The intrinsic carrier uses the supplied underived module-sheaf and differential interfaces. Its local formulas must respect restrictions, tensor identifications and equality detection before any affine computation becomes a sheaf theorem. The reserved general-site integrable parameter-connection definition is part of this layer, not a synonym for a coordinate matrix.

Ordered iteration and symmetric action are separate constructions. Joint nilpotence may be checked in coordinates without integrability; an action of the symmetric algebra requires commuting contractions. The tensor nilpotence bound is N+M−1 for positive input bounds. The added shuffle construction proves the genuine tensor-valued formula over arbitrary commutative rings and arbitrary coefficient modules; it is stronger than the earlier dual-contraction, finite-basis and finite-projective routes. Its empty-word and slot-order tests determine the convention.

The additional field and reduced-ring rank bounds are now explicit targets, rather than historical continuation leads. They require commuting nilpotent contractions and the stated rank/reducedness hypotheses. The residue construction takes the quotient of an additive parameter-t connection. It gives an R-linear quotient map even when dt≠0; it does not silently identify that quotient with a chosen differential fibre. These additions refine the original H.0 frontier while leaving global sheaf transport, determinant descent, cross-ring exterior comparison and the unbounded period lattice open.

**Atlas landmarks.** [Joint Higgs nilpotence](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-joint-nilpotence), [Higgs and λ-connections](#node-hodgestructurespartii-key-higgs-parameter-connections), [Twisted Higgs bundles](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-twisted-higgs), [Griffiths filtrations](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-griffiths-filtration), [Graded Higgs field](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-graded-higgs), [Rees parameter connection](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-rees-parameter).

### Affine and intrinsic operator library

### TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-coordinate-frame"></a>

#### Commuting coordinate directions with constant parameter

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/coordinate-frame` · definition · planning target

Frame consists of d k-linear derivations δ_i:R→R, pairwise commuting on every a∈R, with δ_i(λ)=0. This is a specified affine frame, not a definition of a general differential site.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:Derivation`, `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`, `mathlib:MvPolynomial.pderiv`, `mathlib:MvPolynomial.derivation_ext`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the pinned Derivation carrier and record its pairwise commutation and constant-parameter equations.
2. Zero derivations give Frame.zero. On k[X_0,…,X_(d−1)], partial derivatives give Frame.polynomial with constant parameter C(c).
3. Prove polynomial commutation on monomials: successive removal of i,j has the same coefficient in both orders, including i=j; extend by k-linearity. Constants differentiate to zero.
4. Frame.one keeps the directions and uses δ_i(1)=0. No invertibility of λ is assumed.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- λ=X_0 with δ_0=∂_0 is excluded over Q since δ_0λ=1.
- Zero directions are allowed, but are not universal differential forms.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Frame`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Frame.zero` (constructor): The all-zero directions give a frame for every d and λ.
- `Frame.polynomial` (constructor): The d-variable polynomial ring with partial derivatives and parameter C(c) gives a frame.
- `Frame.one` (constructor): Replace λ by 1 without changing directions.
- `Frame.zero_delta` (simp): Every zero-frame direction acts by zero.
- `Frame.polynomial_delta` (compatibility): The ith polynomial-frame direction is exactly MvPolynomial.pderiv i.
- `Frame.one_delta` (simp): The one-parameter frame has the input directions.
- `Frame.ext` (extensionality): For fixed k,R,d,λ, two frames with the same derivation in each direction are equal; commutation and relative constancy are proof fields.

**Unit tests.**

- `Frame.test_zero` (degenerate): In the one-direction zero frame, δ_0(a)=0 for every a.
- `Frame.test_polynomial_X` (computation): Over Q[X] with constant parameter 1, δ_0(X)=1.
- `Frame.test_identity_not_derivation` (non-example): Over Q, 1≠1·1+1·1; the identity map cannot satisfy the derivation Leibniz rule.
- `Frame.test_variable_parameter` (non-example): Over Q[X] with λ=X, no frame can have δ₀=∂/∂X, because δ₀(λ)=1≠0. This tests the constant-parameter field itself.

**Consumers.**

- `HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0 reserved general Higgs/parameter interface`: Provides local discriminating tests and transport formulas, not a substitute for intrinsic forms, sheaf descent or finite locally free coefficients.
- `EG20 §4.2; LZ17 Remark 3.2`: Checks the constant-parameter Leibniz equation and its specializations before any comparison theorem.

**Sources.**

- [design/EG-author-2026](#source-design-eg-author-2026): Author-hosted 44-page copy, §4.2 printed pp.23–24, parameter Leibniz equation and zero/one fibers; §2.1 printed pp.5–6, Higgs integrability equation. The source gives the parameter Leibniz equation and Higgs/ordinary specializations. Its opening definition allows a regular-function parameter; this node uses the explicitly stated relatively constant restriction. The arbitrary-ring or ringed-site construction is an authored algebraic deduction, not a source theorem at that generality.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-preconnection"></a>

#### Affine coordinate parameter connection

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/preconnection` · definition · planning target

For a fixed Frame F, Connection is a family A_i∈Mat_V(R). It encodes D_i(s)=λδ_i(s)+A_i s before imposing flatness. F is an explicit type parameter: changing the directions or parameter is not a silent type identification.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/coordinate-frame`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-coordinate-frame).

**Proof route.**

1. Use the matrix family as the sole data field.
2. Keep F explicitly in the structure declaration even though the matrix field alone does not mention F.
3. Construct zero matrices. Extensionality and constructor projection follow from the product representation.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- No flatness or nilpotence is imposed on an arbitrary Connection.
- Any one-direction rank-one matrix family is accepted, including a nonzero scalar.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Connection.zero` (constructor): All zero matrices define a preconnection.
- `Connection.zero_matrix` (simp): The ith matrix of the zero preconnection is zero.
- `Connection.matrix_ext` (extensionality): Agreement of all matrices implies equality for the same F,V.
- `Connection.mk_matrix` (projection): The constructor on a family A projects to A_i.

**Unit tests.**

- `Connection.test_zero_matrix` (degenerate): Zero preconnection projects to zero.
- `Connection.test_constructor_projection` (characterisation): The ith projection of the constructor on A is A_i.
- `Connection.test_rank_one` (computation): Over Q with one zero direction, the supplied 1×1 matrix is unchanged by construction and projection.

**Consumers.**

- `HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0 reserved general Higgs/parameter interface`: Provides local discriminating tests and transport formulas, not a substitute for intrinsic forms, sheaf descent or finite locally free coefficients.
- `EG20 §4.2; LZ17 Remark 3.2`: Checks the constant-parameter Leibniz equation and its specializations before any comparison theorem.

The source gives the parameter Leibniz equation and Higgs/ordinary specializations. <a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator"></a>

#### Coordinate parameter differential operator

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator` · construction · planning target

Define the k-linear operator (D_i s)_v=λδ_i(s_v)+(A_i s)_v. It satisfies D_i(a s)=aD_i(s)+λδ_i(a)s and is generally not R-linear.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/preconnection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-preconnection), `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`, `mathlib:Matrix.mulVec`.

**Proof route.**

1. Apply the derivation in each coordinate, multiply by λ and add the matrix-vector action.
2. k-linearity follows from derivation k-linearity and R-linear matrix multiplication.
3. Expand δ_i(a s_v) using Leibniz and scalar commutation to get precisely one λ in the scalar derivative term.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Zero matrices give λδ, not the zero operator in general.
- At λ=1 the scalar derivative is the ordinary connection term.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.operator`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Connection.operator_apply` (projection): D_i(s)=λδ_i(s)+A_i s coordinatewise.
- `Connection.operator_leibniz` (characterisation): D_i(a s)=aD_i(s)+λδ_i(a)s.
- `Connection.operator_zero` (simp): Zero matrices give D_i(s)=λδ_i(s).

**Unit tests.**

- `Connection.test_operator_zero_section` (degenerate): D_i(0)=0.
- `Connection.test_operator_unit` (computation): The zero-matrix model acts by λδ_i in every coordinate.
- `Connection.test_operator_polynomial_leibniz` (computation): Over Q[X] with λ=1 and A=0, D(Xs)=XD(s)+s.
- `Connection.test_operator_parameter_two` (non-example): On Q[X] with λ=2 and zero matrix, D(X)=2, not the ordinary derivative value 1.

**Consumers.**

- `HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0 reserved general Higgs/parameter interface`: Provides local discriminating tests and transport formulas, not a substitute for intrinsic forms, sheaf descent or finite locally free coefficients.
- `EG20 §4.2; LZ17 Remark 3.2`: Checks the constant-parameter Leibniz equation and its specializations before any comparison theorem.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature"></a>

#### Coordinate curvature matrix

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature` · definition · planning target

Define κ_ij=λδ_i(A_j)−λδ_j(A_i)+A_i A_j−A_j A_i with entrywise derivatives. In a genuine polynomial coordinate chart the two-form is Σ_(i<j)κ_ij dx_i∧dx_j.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/preconnection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-preconnection), `mathlib:Matrix.single`.

**Proof route.**

1. Construct the displayed matrix expression using entrywise derivations.
2. Unfold to show κ_ii=0, κ_ji=−κ_ij and vanishing curvature for zero matrices.
3. For E12,E21 multiply E12 E21=E11 and E21 E12=E22; constant matrices have zero derivatives.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- On Q[x,y], E12 dx+E21 dy has curvature diag(1,−1)dx∧dy.
- The zero-direction Q test reproduces the same matrix coefficient without claiming universal forms.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.curvature`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Connection.curvature_self` (simp): κ_ii=0.
- `Connection.curvature_swap` (relation): κ_ji=−κ_ij.
- `Connection.curvature_zero` (simp): All zero matrices have zero curvature.

**Unit tests.**

- `Connection.test_curvature_self` (degenerate): Every diagonal-direction curvature is zero.
- `Connection.test_curvature_zero` (degenerate): All curvatures of zero matrices vanish.
- `Connection.test_curvature_noncommuting` (computation): With two zero directions over Q, λ=0, A_0=E12 and A_1=E21, κ_01=diag(1,−1).

**Consumers.**

- `HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0 reserved general Higgs/parameter interface`: Provides local discriminating tests and transport formulas, not a substitute for intrinsic forms, sheaf descent or finite locally free coefficients.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator-commutator"></a>

#### Commutator is curvature action

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator-commutator` · theorem · planning target

For every c,i,j and s∈R^V, D_i(D_j(s))−D_j(D_i(s))=κ_ij s.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature), `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`, `mathlib:Matrix.mulVec_mulVec`.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand both compositions, including derivatives of λ and all matrix entries.
2. The second derivatives cancel by Frame.commute. Terms λδ_i(λ)δ_j(s) vanish by Frame.constant.
3. Use Leibniz inside finite sums; mixed A_iδ_j(s) terms cancel and remaining entries equal κ_ij s.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Without δλ=0 an extra term is λ(δ_iλ·δ_j(s)−δ_jλ·δ_i(s)).
- The E12/E21 commutator acts by diag(1,−1).

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-flatness"></a>

#### Flatness of the coordinate model

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/flatness` · definition · planning target

Connection.IsFlat means κ_ij=0 for every i,j. It is equivalent to pairwise commuting D_i on every section, and does not assert nilpotence.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator-commutator`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator-commutator).

**Proof route.**

1. Define the predicate by the explicit curvature equalities.
2. The commutator theorem proves one direction.
3. For the converse evaluate the zero operator on each coordinate basis vector; every column of κ_ij vanishes.
4. For d=1 the only curvature is diagonal and hence zero.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A scalar Higgs coefficient 1 on A¹_Q is flat but not nilpotent.
- Two directions with E12,E21 fail flatness.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.IsFlat`.

- `Connection.isFlat_zero` (simp): The zero preconnection is flat.
- `Connection.isFlat_one_direction` (characterisation): Every one-direction model is flat.

- `Connection.test_flat_line` (computation): Every one-direction model is flat.
- `Connection.test_flat_noncommuting` (non-example): The two-direction E12,E21 model over Q is not flat.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-gauge"></a>

#### Coordinate change by an invertible matrix

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/gauge` · construction · planning target

For a matrix unit G and the convention s′=Gs, define A′_i=G A_i G^−1−λδ_i(G)G^−1. The associated operator is G D_i G^−1 on the new component column.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

3. Its operator commutator is G[D_i,D_j]G^−1. Use the commutator node and coordinate basis evaluation to identify κ′_ij=Gκ_ijG^−1.
4. Invertibility of G proves preservation and reflection of curvature vanishing.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-tensor"></a>

#### Tensor with the same parameter

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/tensor` · construction · planning target

For models c on R^V and b on R^W with the same F and λ, construct the free model on R^(V×W) with matrices A_i⊗I_W+I_V⊗B_i, using the Kronecker product. Its parameter is λ, not 2λ.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the standard free-coordinate tensor identification and define the Kronecker sum.
2. Entrywise differentiate; the cross commutators cancel since A⊗I commutes with I⊗B. The remaining curvature is κ_c⊗I+I⊗κ_b.
3. On elementary tensors, λδ(s⊗t)=λδ(s)⊗t+s⊗λδ(t). Scalar balancing identifies the derivative term represented in either factor, so one λ occurs.
4. Vanishing of both input curvatures implies vanishing of the tensor curvature; no converse is claimed.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Input parameters must agree.
- The balanced tensor scalar Leibniz rule has one λ derivative term.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.tensor`.

- `Connection.tensor_curvature` (compatibility): Tensor curvature is κ_c,ij⊗I_W+I_V⊗κ_b,ij.
- `Connection.tensor_flat` (compatibility): Flat inputs give a flat tensor.

- `Connection.test_tensor_flat` (compatibility): The tensor of flat models is flat.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-dual"></a>

#### Coordinate dual parameter connection

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/dual` · construction · planning target

Identify the dual of R^V with row coefficients transposed to a column, and define the dual matrix as −A_iᵀ. Keep the same F and λ.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand the evaluation-pairing equation λδ_i(φ(s))=D_dual,i(φ)(s)+φ(D_i(s)); its coefficient terms force −A_iᵀ.
2. Entrywise differentiation and reversal of products under transpose give κ_dual,ij=−κ_ijᵀ.
3. Double transposition recovers A, and curvature vanishing is preserved.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Omitting the minus sign breaks compatibility with evaluation.
- This coordinate identification is only for finite free modules, not a claimed sheaf-duality construction.

- `Connection.test_dual_involution` (compatibility): Taking the dual twice returns c.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-invertible-rescale"></a>

#### Rescaling an invertible parameter

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/invertible-rescale` · construction · planning target

For u∈R× and F with λ=u, define rescale(c) on F.one by matrices u^−1A_i. Its operator is u^−1D_i and curvature u^−2κ_ij; its scalar Leibniz coefficient is 1.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/coordinate-frame`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-coordinate-frame), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/flatness`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-flatness), `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`.

**Proof route.**

1. Differentiate u u^−1=1 and use δ_i(u)=0 to obtain δ_i(u^−1)=0.
2. Retain the same directions with parameter 1 and multiply every coefficient matrix by u^−1.
3. The new operator is δ_i(s)+u^−1A_i s=u^−1D_i(s). Expanding curvature scales derivative and commutator terms by u^−2.
4. Invertibility makes flatness equivalent. Merely changing λ's type while leaving A unscaled is incorrect.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Over Q[X], the zero-matrix λ=2 model maps X to 2; rescaling maps X to 1.
- λ=0 and nonunit parameters do not admit this operation.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.rescale`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Connection.rescale_matrix` (projection): The rescaled matrix is u^−1A_i.
- `Connection.rescale_operator` (compatibility): The rescaled operator is u^−1D_i.
- `Connection.rescale_curvature` (compatibility): The rescaled curvature is u^−2κ_ij.

**Unit tests.**

- `Connection.test_rescale_flat` (compatibility): Rescaling preserves flatness.
- `Connection.test_rescale_zero` (degenerate): Zero matrices rescale to zero matrices.
- `Connection.test_rescale_leibniz` (characterisation): D_rescale,i(a s)=aD_rescale,i(s)+δ_i(a)s.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-joint-nilpotence"></a>

#### Joint word nilpotence of Higgs coefficients

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/joint-nilpotence` · definition · planning target

At λ=0, JointNilpotent(c,N) means N>0 and A_(i1)…A_(iN)=0 for every direction word of length N. This is a separate finite bound; no rank-one-zero assertion over nonreduced R is made.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type. Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/preconnection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-preconnection), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/dual`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-dual), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/flatness`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-flatness), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/zero-parameter-curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-zero-parameter-curvature), `mathlib:Matrix.single`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use all words of length N, not exterior products, and require N>0.
2. Zero matrices satisfy bound 1; one-letter words show that bound 1 iff every A_i=0.
3. For the dual a product equals (−1)^N times the transpose of the reversed original word, hence the same bound holds.
4. Compute E12²=0≠E12 and scalar ε²=0≠ε examples. The scalar 1 has nonzero word product at every positive length.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Scalar 1 in one direction over Q is flat but has no finite bound.
- For ε²=0≠ε in nonreduced R, a rank-one coefficient ε is nonzero with bound 2.
- The intrinsic finite-filtration comparison and tensor nilpotence bounds are now planned by H.0/nilpotence-equivalence and H.0/tensor-nilpotence; the exact E1 tensor-kernel contract and their global Lean signatures remain outstanding.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.JointNilpotent`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Connection.jointNilpotent_zero` (simp): Zero matrices have bound 1.
- `Connection.jointNilpotent_dual` (compatibility): Duality preserves the stated bound N.
- `Connection.jointNilpotent_one_iff` (characterisation): Bound 1 iff every matrix is zero.

**Unit tests.**

- `Connection.test_nilpotent_nonzero` (computation): In one direction over Q, E12 on Q² has bound 2 but is nonzero.
- `Connection.test_integrable_not_nilpotent` (non-example): The one-direction scalar 1 over Q is flat but not JointNilpotent(c,N) for any N.
- `Connection.test_nonreduced_rank_one` (computation): If ε²=0≠ε in R, the one-direction rank-one scalar ε model has bound 2 but is nonzero.

**Consumers.**

- `HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0 general Higgs/parameter interface`: Pins local transport and specialization tests without substituting for global sheaf descent.
- `LZ17 Remark 1.10 and Theorem 2.1`: Distinguishes a separate finite nilpotence condition from integrability and keeps the coefficient ring visible.

### TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-intrinsic-preconnection"></a>

#### Intrinsic parameter preconnections

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/intrinsic-preconnection` · definition · planning target

A Preconnection(E,λ) is an additive map of sheaves D:E→E⊗_OΩ¹ satisfying D(ae)=aD(e)+λ(e⊗da) on every object after local restriction. It is not O-linear unless its Leibniz correction vanishes. Integrability is a separate predicate; neither a lattice nor trace-zero nor nilpotence is part of this carrier.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:SheafOfModules`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the native module-sheaf carrier and imported sheaf tensor. Define D as a morphism of underlying abelian sheaves.
2. Impose the displayed local Leibniz equality, compatible with all restrictions. This automatically gives linearity over the relatively constant base.
3. Equality of D as an additive sheaf map gives equality of preconnections; construction requires actual data and the equality, not a supplied unnamed proposition.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A Preconnection(E,λ) is an additive map of sheaves D:E→E⊗_OΩ¹ satisfying D(ae)=aD(e)+λ(e⊗da) on every object after local restriction. It is not O-linear unless its Leibniz correction vanishes. Integrability is a separate predicate; neither a lattice nor trace-zero nor nilpotence is part of this carrier.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Higgs/ParameterConnection`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection`; declaration: `Preconnection`.

**Reusable API.**

- `Preconnection.mk` (constructor): An additive sheaf map and its λ-Leibniz proof give a preconnection.
- `Preconnection.leibniz` (projection): D(ae)=aD(e)+λ(e⊗da).
- `Preconnection.ext` (extensionality): Equal section maps on all site objects imply equality.
- `Preconnection.base_linear` (compatibility): D(be)=bD(e) whenever db=0.

**Unit tests.**

- `Preconnection.test_affine_line` (computation): On A¹_k, λd on O sends x to λdx.
- `Preconnection.test_zero_parameter` (degenerate): At λ=0 the correction is zero and D is O-linear.
- `Preconnection.test_not_O_linear` (non-example): Over Q[x], d(x·1)=dx while x d(1)=0, so the unit ordinary connection is not O-linear.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-extension-balancing"></a>

#### Balancing the exterior extension

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/extension-balancing` · lemma · planning target

For n≥0, B_n(e,ω)=D(e)∧ω+λe⊗dω is biadditive and O-balanced: B_n(ae,ω)=B_n(e,aω). In degree zero use E⊗O≅E. No O-linearity of B_n in an individual argument is assumed.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/intrinsic-preconnection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-intrinsic-preconnection), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`, `mathlib:TensorProduct.liftAddHom`, [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/exterior-extension-pair-apply`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-exterior-extension-pair-apply).

**Proof route.**

1. Expand B_n(ae,ω) using the λ-Leibniz rule.
2. Expand d(aω)=da∧ω+a dω; the two derivative terms coincide, and bilinearity moves a between factors.
3. Both expressions are aD(e)∧ω+λe⊗da∧ω+λae⊗dω. Additivity is inherited from D,d and wedge.
4. The new affine extensionPair evaluation supplies the degree-one component; prove its balance from the same λ-Leibniz and d₁-Leibniz terms. This does not establish native sheaf restriction/gluing.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For n≥0, B_n(e,ω)=D(e)∧ω+λe⊗dω is biadditive and O-balanced: B_n(ae,ω)=B_n(e,aω). In degree zero use E⊗O≅E. No O-linearity of B_n in an individual argument is assumed.

#### Extended parameter differential

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/exterior-extension` · construction · planning target

E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature-linearity"></a>

#### Curvature is O-linear

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature-linearity` · lemma · planning target

For relatively constant λ, κ_D(ae)=aκ_D(e). If dλ is not assumed zero the extra term is e⊗λdλ∧da. Thus κ_D is canonically an O-linear sheaf morphism under the standing hypotheses.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/intrinsic-curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-intrinsic-curvature), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/exterior-extension`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-exterior-extension), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-curvature-scalar-defect`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-affine-curvature-scalar-defect).

**Proof route.**

1. Expand D_1(aD(e)) with its scalar rule.
2. Expand D_1(λe⊗da). The mixed terms λD(e)∧da and its reversed wedge cancel; d²a=0.
3. The remaining scalar defect is λe⊗dλ∧da, which vanishes by relative constancy.
4. The new actual affine defect formula reduces to scalar linearity when d₀λ=0. Transport to the general ringed-site carrier still requires the exact E1 restriction and equality-detection interfaces.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For relatively constant λ, κ_D(ae)=aκ_D(e). If dλ is not assumed zero the extra term is e⊗λdλ∧da. Thus κ_D is canonically an O-linear sheaf morphism under the standing hypotheses.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-flat-extension-square"></a>

#### Flatness in every exterior degree

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/flat-extension-square` · theorem · planning target

For dλ=0, D_{n+1}D_n(e⊗ω)=κ_D(e)∧ω for every n. Hence κ_D=0 iff all adjacent extended differentials compose to zero.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/exterior-extension`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-exterior-extension), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/intrinsic-curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-intrinsic-curvature).

**Proof route.**

1. Apply the extension formula twice. The D(e)∧dω terms cancel with the degree-one sign.
2. Use d²ω=0 and dλ=0; retain exactly D_1D(e)∧ω.
3. Local elementary tensors generate the sheaf tensor, and n=0 gives the converse.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For dλ=0, D_{n+1}D_n(e⊗ω)=κ_D(e)∧ω for every n. Hence κ_D=0 iff all adjacent extended differentials compose to zero.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-key-higgs-parameter-connections"></a>

#### Integrable parameter bundles

`HodgeStructuresPartII:key/higgs-parameter-connections` · definition · planning target

LambdaBundle(Ω,λ) consists of a finite locally free O-module sheaf E and a Preconnection(E,λ) with κ_D=0. The parameter is a central relatively constant global section. This is the reserved general ringed-site definition: at λ=0 it gives integrable Higgs bundles and at λ=1 the imported ordinary connection carrier. Tensor, dual, pullback, coefficient twists and Griffiths grading are provided by the declaration nodes below; they are not axioms stored as arbitrary properties of an object.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Proof route.**

1. Take E in the native sheaf category with a covering family on which E has a finite basis. The family need not be finite, and the finite local rank may vary between its members. Do not require a finite trivializing cover, a globally bounded rank, or a global basis.
2. Bundle actual additive D with its Leibniz proof and its defined curvature equality.
3. Use the extension-square theorem to give a genuine complex. λ=1 comparisons use the CR.1 carrier; general Higgs structure is the zero fiber of the same definition.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- LambdaBundle(Ω,λ) consists of a finite locally free O-module sheaf E and a Preconnection(E,λ) with κ_D=0. The parameter is a central relatively constant global section. This is the reserved general ringed-site definition: at λ=0 it gives integrable Higgs bundles and at λ=1 the imported ordinary connection carrier. Tensor, dual, pullback, coefficient twists and Griffiths grading are provided by the declaration nodes below; they are not axioms stored as arbitrary properties of an object.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Higgs/ParameterConnection`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection`; declaration: `LambdaBundle`.

**Reusable API.**

- `LambdaBundle.mk` (constructor): Bundle E,D, finite local freeness, and the actual curvature-zero equality.
- `LambdaBundle.connection` (projection): Recover D with its λ-Leibniz rule.
- `LambdaBundle.integrable` (projection): The defined exterior curvature is zero.
- `LambdaBundle.ext` (extensionality): For the same underlying E, equal additive D gives equal bundle structures.
- `LambdaBundle.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction to a slice/open subsite retains the same parameter and integrability.
- `LambdaBundle.test_criterion_nilpotence` (example): On A¹_Q the Higgs line θ=dx is integrable and satisfies θ^[N\](1)=1⊗dx^⊗N≠0 for each N>0. Integrability is not ordered tensor nilpotence.
- `LambdaBundle.rescale_equiv` (equivalence): For invertible λ with dλ=0, λ⁻¹D is an ordinary integrable connection. Scaling by λ and λ⁻¹ are inverse functors; supplied by H.0/intrinsic-rescale.
- `LambdaBundle.tensor_leibniz` (compatibility): Same-λ tensor uses D_E⊗1+1⊗D_F and has scalar correction λ(e⊗f)⊗da, with one λ; supplied by H.0/intrinsic-tensor.
- `LambdaBundle.dual_eval` (compatibility): (D∨φ)(e)=λd(φ(e))−φ(D(e)); for dλ=0 the dual is integrable, supplied by H.0/intrinsic-dual and H.0/dual-curvature.
- `LambdaBundle.pullback_apply` (functoriality): For a differential-site morphism with compatible exterior map, D_Y(b⊗e)=λ_Y e⊗d_Yb+b df(D_Xe), and integrability is preserved; supplied by H.0/intrinsic-pullback.
- `GriffithsFiltration.gradedHiggs_linear` (compatibility): For a flat ordinary bundle with the bounded Griffiths filtration of H.0/griffiths-filtration, θ_p([e])=[∇e] is O-linear and its exterior square is zero; supplied by H.0/graded-higgs and H.0/graded-higgs-integrable.

**Unit tests.**

- `LambdaBundle.test_affine_unit` (computation): For a field k, on A¹_k the ordinary differential (O,d) is a nonzero rank-one flat connection; at λ=0 the field θ=dx is an integrable rank-one Higgs object.
- `LambdaBundle.test_parameter_unit` (compatibility): D=λd for constant λ is flat, with λ=1 giving d and λ=0 giving the zero Higgs field.
- `LambdaBundle.test_noncommuting` (non-example): On A²_Q, E12dx+E21dy does not define a LambdaBundle at λ=0.
- `LambdaBundle.test_zero_module` (degenerate): The zero sheaf with its unique operator is admitted, with local rank zero.
- `LambdaBundle.test_integrable_not_nilpotent` (non-example): On A¹_Q the Higgs line θ=dx is integrable, but θ^[N\](1)=1⊗dx^⊗N≠0 for every N>0.
- `LambdaBundle.test_rescale_two` (computation): On Q[x], λ=2 and D=2d give a flat bundle; λ⁻¹D=d and evaluates x to dx.
- `LambdaBundle.test_same_parameter_tensor` (compatibility): On Q[x], tensoring the two unit λ=2 flat lines gives the unit λ=2 line, whose operator on x is 2dx, not 4dx.
- `LambdaBundle.test_dual_pullback` (computation): The Higgs line dx over Q[x] has dual field −dx. Along x=y², the original pulls back to 2y dy and its dual pulls back to −2y dy; both are integrable Higgs lines.
- `LambdaBundle.test_graded_higgs` (computation): On Q[x], ∇=d+E21dx on O² with F¹=Oe₁, F⁰=O² and zero F² gives θ([e₁])=[e₂]dx, θ([e₂])=0. The graded Higgs field is integrable and has ordered bound 2.
- `LambdaBundle.test_locally_varying_rank` (non-example): On the discrete space N with constant ring Q, zero differential calculus and λ=0, the sheaf with stalk Q^n at n and zero Higgs operator is finite locally free and integrable. It has no finite cover by free constant-rank charts because its ranks are unbounded.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-zero-fiber"></a>

#### Higgs zero fiber

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/zero-fiber` · comparison · planning target

At λ=0, preconnections are exactly O-linear fields θ:E→E⊗Ω¹, and κ_D=(id⊗wedge)(θ⊗id)θ. Thus LambdaBundle(Ω,0) is equivalent to the integrable Higgs category, including its horizontal morphisms, without any nilpotence or trace-zero condition.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:key/higgs-parameter-connections`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-key-higgs-parameter-connections), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/connection-morphism`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-connection-morphism), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/exterior-extension`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-exterior-extension).

**Proof route.**

1. The zero-parameter Leibniz rule is exactly O-linearity.
2. In the extension formula the dω term vanishes; the remaining composite is θ∧θ.
3. The two constructions leave the underlying E and map unchanged and are inverse on morphisms.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- At λ=0, preconnections are exactly O-linear fields θ:E→E⊗Ω¹, and κ_D=(id⊗wedge)(θ⊗id)θ. Thus LambdaBundle(Ω,0) is equivalent to the integrable Higgs category, including its horizontal morphisms, without any nilpotence or trace-zero condition.

#### Invertible parameter rescaling

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/intrinsic-rescale` · construction · planning target

If λ is an invertible relatively constant section, rescale by λ⁻¹D to obtain an ordinary integrable connection. Its curvature is λ⁻²κ_D. This gives an equivalence of fixed-λ and ordinary connection categories with inverse ∇↦λ∇, including tensor, dual and horizontal morphisms.

No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Proof route.**

1. Differentiate λλ⁻¹=1 to get dλ⁻¹=0.
2. Expand the scaled Leibniz equation: the scalar derivative coefficient becomes 1.
3. The extended differential scales by λ⁻¹ in every degree, so its square scales by λ⁻². The inverse and morphisms are unchanged on E.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-nilpotence-equivalence"></a>

#### Tensor nilpotence and finite filtrations

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/nilpotence-equivalence` · theorem · planning target

When Q is finite locally free, θ^[N]=0 for N>0 iff a length-N nilpotence filtration exists. No integrability is needed for this equivalence of ordered iterates and lowering filtrations. For a general coherent Q without flatness, this equivalence is not asserted.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor. Q=Ω¹⊗T is finite locally free; E finite locally free, and the tensor-exactness/kernel identification for Q is imported from E1.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/ordered-iterate`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-ordered-iterate), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/nilpotence-filtration`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-nilpotence-filtration), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

**Proof route.**

1. A lowering filtration kills N successive applications on E=K_N.
2. Conversely define K_j=ker θ^[j]. Locally a finite basis of Q identifies K_j with vectors annihilated by all words of length j.
3. These kernels ascend and θ(K_j)⊆K_{j−1}⊗Q: contraction by each basis covector lands in K_{j−1}; finite locally free tensor exactness identifies the kernel after tensoring.
4. K_0=ker id=0 and θ^[N]=0 gives K_N=E; glue kernels without asserting they or their quotients are locally free.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- When Q is finite locally free, θ^[N]=0 for N>0 iff a length-N nilpotence filtration exists. No integrability is needed for this equivalence of ordered iterates and lowering filtrations. For a general coherent Q without flatness, this equivalence is not asserted.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Higgs/ParameterConnection`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection`; declaration: `TwistedHiggsBundle.nilpotence_iff_filtration`.

- [design/LZ17](#source-design-lz17): Theorem 2.1(i),(iii),(iv), PDF p.7; Remark 1.10 p.5. The source requires twisted fields, tensor, dual and pullback. This packet supplies their generic algebra, not the source correspondence or its nilpotence proof.

No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand the (N+M−1)-fold iterate as a sum indexed by choosing the E or F action at every position; distributivity and tensor associators give this formula without a basis of Q.
2. Reorder actions on separate E,F factors while retaining the corresponding permutation of the ordered Q factors. Every summand factors through an E iterate of length r and an F iterate of length s with r+s=N+M−1.
3. Either r≥N or s≥M. Higher iterates factor through the specified zero iterate, so that summand vanishes. This is an integral shuffle argument: no integrability between directions, local freeness of Q or division by binomial coefficients is required.
4. The contraction adapter supplies the necessary N+M−1 bound after evaluating every slot in the same dual direction, and an integral binomial identity for that specialization. Complete the mixed E/F shuffle factorization before concluding actual ordered-tensor vanishing; self-contraction powers do not detect mixed words in characteristic two.
5. The mixed contraction-word expansion now yields the actual affine ordered tensor bound with a chosen finite coefficient basis. It covers arbitrary E,F and arbitrary characteristic without integrability. Remove the coefficient-basis restriction via an actual tensor-valued shuffle and discharge native sheaf restriction/gluing before concluding this unchanged general ringed-site theorem.
6. The actual affine ordered tensor bound N+M−1 now extends from finite-basis coefficients to finite-projective Q by a native finite free retract, and to principal covers with local projective coefficient data. E and F need not be flat. The general arbitrary-Q tensor-valued shuffle, native finite-projective sheaf restriction/tensor-power coherence, equality detection and gluing remain required. These affine results do not identify tensors of global sections with sheaf tensor sections or close the reserved general ringed-site key.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- If two same-Q fields have positive ordered bounds N and M, their tensor field has bound N+M−1. The proof is valid in arbitrary characteristic and over nonreduced rings, without dividing by binomial coefficients.

#### Dual nilpotence bound

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/dual-nilpotence` · theorem · planning target

For finite locally free E,Q, a twisted Higgs field with ordered bound N has a dual field with the same bound N. In a finite local basis, its word equals (−1)^N times the transpose of the reversed original word.

**Hypotheses.** A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition. λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object. Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/ordered-iterate`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-ordered-iterate), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/twisted-higgs`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-twisted-higgs), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the dual evaluation definition to identify each contracted matrix with −A_iᵀ.
2. Multiplication under transpose reverses order, and all reversed words are included in the original bound.
3. Finite local evaluation detects zero and glues the bound.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For finite locally free E,Q, a twisted Higgs field with ordered bound N has a dual field with the same bound N. In a finite local basis, its word equals (−1)^N times the transpose of the reversed original word.

#### Flat connection gives integrable symbol

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/graded-higgs-integrable` · theorem · planning target

The degree −1 associated-graded symbol of a flat Griffiths-transverse connection has θ∧θ=0. Flatness ∇²=0 is essential. This is an exterior-square assertion; finite ordered nilpotence instead follows from filtration bounds.

#### Coordinate determinant parameter connection

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-coordinate` · construction · planning target

For the finite free coordinate model c with matrices A_i, construct a rank-one coordinate model det(c) with the same F and λ and one-by-one matrix tr(A_i). Its section operator is s ↦ λδ_i(s)+tr(A_i)s. This is the local coefficient model for the induced top exterior-power connection; the global determinant sheaf, the wedge identification and change-of-frame descent are separate supplier/bridge obligations. Rank zero gives the unit-line connection with zero coefficient.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. F is the existing coordinate Frame: its k-linear derivations commute and annihilate λ. Every coordinate model uses this same frame. The index types V and W are finite decidable types. No positive rank, characteristic-zero or invertibility of rank is assumed.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/preconnection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-preconnection), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator), `mathlib:Matrix.trace`.

**Proof route.**

1. Define the rank-one matrices by the existing matrix trace, summing diagonal entries; reuse the existing coordinate Connection carrier with index Fin 1.
2. The operator formula follows from the existing operator equation. The scalar derivative term has λ, not rank(V)λ; the rank only multiplies scalar coefficient matrices.
3. This construction uses no scalar division, exterior-sheaf construction or global frame choice. Its identification with a top exterior power is recorded as a separate gap, not an assumed theorem.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Distinguish trace(A_i) from the algebraic determinant of A_i.
- The model preserves the source parameter at every rank, including rank zero.
- Trace loses information: flatness of det(c) has no converse.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-gauge-curvature"></a>

#### Curvature under coordinate change

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/gauge-curvature` · lemma · planning target

For the coordinate transformation s′=Gs and every invertible matrix G, curvature transforms as κ_gauge(c,G),ij=G κ_c,ij G⁻¹. This is the promoted curvature API of the inherited gauge construction.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. F is the existing coordinate Frame: its k-linear derivations commute and annihilate λ. Every coordinate model uses this same frame. The index types V and W are finite decidable types. No positive rank, characteristic-zero or invertibility of rank is assumed.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/gauge`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-gauge), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/curvature`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-curvature), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/coordinate-frame`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-coordinate-frame), `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`.

**Proof route.**

1. Differentiate GG⁻¹=I entrywise. The matrix product Leibniz rule gives δ_i(G⁻¹)=−G⁻¹δ_i(G)G⁻¹ by multiplying the resulting zero identity on the left by G⁻¹.
2. Insert the defined coefficient G A_i G⁻¹−λδ_i(G)G⁻¹ into the curvature formula. Use the preceding inverse derivative, the relatively constant parameter and commutation of the coordinate derivations to cancel all terms with derivatives of G; the remaining expression is G(λδ_iA_j−λδ_jA_i+[A_i,A_j])G⁻¹. Finite matrix sums and multiplication are over the commutative ring R.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The transformation convention is s′=Gs, so the derivative correction has a minus sign.
- No field, characteristic-zero hypothesis or matrix inverse in a field is used: G is a unit of the matrix ring.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-derivation-rows"></a>

#### Derivation of a determinant by row replacements

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-derivation-rows` · lemma · planning target

For a k-linear derivation δ:R→R and any square matrix S, δ(det S)=Σ_r det(updateRow S r (j↦δ(S_rj))). S need not be invertible.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:Derivation.leibniz`, `mathlib:Derivation.map_intCast`, `mathlib:Derivation.map_one_eq_zero`, `mathlib:Matrix.det_apply'`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the pinned det_apply' permutation formula. Additivity moves δ through the finite sum; Derivation.map_intCast kills each integer-valued permutation sign.
2. Induct over the finite product for each permutation: δ(Π_j S_(σj),j)=Σ_j δ(S_(σj),j) Π_{l≠j} S_(σl),l. The empty product derivative is δ(1)=0. This is an induction using the existing Leibniz rule, not a new generic product carrier.
3. For a fixed permutation, the row-replacement determinant has exactly one differentiated factor, in the column j=σ⁻¹(r). Reindex the finite row sum r=σ(j), then exchange the permutation and column sums. The permutation sign is unchanged.
4. No inverse is introduced. The argument also works for singular matrices, repeated rows and characteristic two; do not prove alternating vanishing by cancelling 2.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The 0×0 determinant is 1, whose derivative and empty row sum are zero.
- For S=diag(x,x) over F₂[x], δ(det S)=δ(x²)=0, and the two replacement terms cancel in characteristic two.
- The formula applies to singular matrices; invertibility is added only at the unit Jacobi node.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `det_derivation_rows`.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-row-action"></a>

#### Trace of infinitesimal left row action

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-row-action` · lemma · planning target

For square matrices A and S over R, Σ_r det(updateRow S r ((A*S)r)) = tr(A) det(S). S is arbitrary, including singular matrices.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:Matrix.det_updateRow_add`, `mathlib:Matrix.det_updateRow_smul`, `mathlib:Matrix.det_updateRow_eq_zero`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace`.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand (A*S)_r=Σ_j A_rj • S_j using the native matrix multiplication finite sum.
2. For each fixed replacement row r, use determinant additivity and scalar linearity in that row to move this sum outside: Σ_j A_rj det(updateRow S r S_j). Finite-sum linearity follows by induction from det_updateRow_add and det_updateRow_smul.
3. If j≠r, the replacement matrix has rows j and r equal, so det_updateRow_eq_zero applies. This native alternating lemma works in characteristic two without dividing by 2.
4. The only surviving term is j=r, with updateRow S r S_r=S. Sum A_rr det(S) over r and identify the diagonal sum with Matrix.trace. In rank zero both sides vanish.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For A=diag(a,b) and S=diag(x,y), the sum is (a+b)xy.
- An off-diagonal elementary A has trace zero, and every nonzero candidate replacement term has duplicated rows.
- Do not confuse this statement with Tau Ceti's existing column-weight identity sum_det_updateRow_mul_row, whose replacement entries are d_j S_rj, not (A*S)_rj.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-gauge-matrix"></a>

#### Determinant coefficient under coordinate change

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-gauge-matrix` · lemma · planning target

For the inherited convention s′=Gs and frame F, (det(c.gauge G)).matrix_i,0,0 = tr(A_i) − λ det(G⁻¹) δ_i(det G). The determinant connection coefficient is not generally gauge invariant.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used. F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-matrix`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-matrix), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/gauge`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-gauge), `ColemanPowerSeries:L1/derivation-determinant-unit`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace_units_conj`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace_sub`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace_smul`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace_mul_comm`.

3. Import ColemanPowerSeries:L1/derivation-determinant-unit with δ=F.delta i and use the pinned Matrix.trace_mul_comm to match its G⁻¹δG trace orientation. Multiply its identity by det(G⁻¹), using determinant multiplicativity and the matrix-unit inverse law; this logarithmic form converts the trace of the derivative correction into det(G⁻¹)δ_i(det G).
4. Keep the minus sign dictated by s′=Gs, and retain λ rather than rank·λ. For λ=0 the derivative term vanishes; this is the conjugation-only Higgs specialization.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-gauge"></a>

#### Determinant connection commutes with gauge transport

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-gauge` · theorem · planning target

Let g=Units.map Matrix.detMonoidHom G∈Rˣ, and let ℓ(g)=Units.map (Matrix.scalar (Fin 1)).toMonoidHom g be the native one-by-one matrix unit. Then (c.gauge G).determinant = c.determinant.gauge ℓ(g), with the same F and λ.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used. F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-gauge-matrix`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-gauge-matrix), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-matrix`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-matrix), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/gauge`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-gauge), `mathlib:Matrix.det_mul`, `mathlib:Matrix.detMonoidHom`, `mathlib:Matrix.scalar`, `mathlib:Units.map`, `mathlib:Units.coe_map`.

**Proof route.**

1. Build g and ℓ(g) only by the existing native monoid homomorphisms and Units.map. Units.coe_map exposes values det G and scalar(det G); inverse values are det(G⁻¹) and scalar(det(G⁻¹)). No new determinant-line carrier or arbitrary choice is introduced.
2. Apply the inherited gauge_matrix formula to the one-by-one determinant connection. Its coefficient is (det G) tr(A_i) det(G⁻¹) − λ δ_i(det G)det(G⁻¹).
3. Use det_mul and the inverse equation to simplify the conjugation scalar product to tr(A_i). Commutativity reorders the derivative factors; determinant-gauge-matrix supplies equality with the left side.
4. Connections are determined by their matrix field. Extensionality over directions and the unique Fin 1 row and column proves equality of coordinate connection objects. Their operator compatibility then follows from the inherited operator definition.
5. This is exact finite-coordinate frame coherence. It does not construct exterior-power sheaves or glue local operators; those remain E1/global-comparison obligations.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The transformation uses det G, not tr G, and exactly the existing gauge convention.
- A nonconstant diagonal Laurent gauge reproduces the negative logarithmic derivative term on both sides.
- The rank-zero vector frame maps to the identity one-by-one frame on the unit line.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Hodge/ParameterConnection/Affine`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.ParameterConnection.Affine`; declaration: `Connection.determinant_gauge`.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-alternating-operator"></a>

#### Alternating determinant evaluation intertwines the section operator

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-alternating-operator` · theorem · planning target

Represent an ordered family of sections as the rows of S. For each direction i, Σ_r det(updateRow S r (c.operator i (S r))) = c.determinant.operator i (fun _↦det S) 0 = λδ_i(det S)+tr(A_i)det S. No flatness or invertibility of S is assumed.

**Hypotheses.** k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear. V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used. F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/operator`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-operator), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-coordinate`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-coordinate), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-derivation-rows`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-derivation-rows), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/determinant-row-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-determinant-row-action), `mathlib:Matrix.det_updateRow_add`, `mathlib:Matrix.det_updateRow_smul`, `mathlib:Matrix.det_transpose`, `mathlib:Matrix.trace_transpose`.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand each section operator as λδ_i(S_r)+A_i*ᵥS_r. Use determinant linearity in the replaced row to split the derivative and matrix-action sums.
2. Pull λ out of each derivative replacement using det_updateRow_smul. The determinant-derivation-rows identity reduces that sum to λδ_i(det S).
3. For any perturbation matrix H, the sum of single-row replacement determinants Σ_r det(updateRow S r H_r) equals the sum of single-column replacement determinants Σ_j det(updateCol S j (r↦H_rj)). Expand det_apply' on both sides: each permutation term replaces exactly one entry S_(σj),j by H_(σj),j, and the row index is reindexed as r=σ(j). No derivation or invertibility is needed for this finite-sum reindexing.
4. For H_r=A_i*ᵥS_r, entrywise H=S*A_iᵀ, not A_i*S. Convert its replacement-row sum to the preceding replacement-column sum, transpose each determinant, and observe Hᵀ=A_i*Sᵀ. The determinant-row-action node with A_i and Sᵀ now gives tr(A_i)det(Sᵀ)=tr(A_i)det S. This explicitly justifies the column-vector/row-family orientation; duplicate-row vanishing, not cancellation by 2, handles every characteristic.
5. Apply determinant_operator to identify the resulting scalar with the one-by-one line section operator. The empty family evaluates to det(∅)=1 and both sides are zero because δ_i(1)=0.
6. This is the local alternating universal-property test needed by a future top-wedge comparison. It is not yet a connection on a global exterior-power module/sheaf.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- With S=diag(x,y), λ=1, δ=∂x and A=diag(a,b), both sides equal y+(a+b)xy.
- For an off-diagonal A, the action part is zero on every S, not merely invertible S.
- Rank zero gives the derivative of the unit section, not a zero determinant line.

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-contractions` · construction · planning target

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. #### Symmetric action on an affine Higgs module

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-symmetric-action` · construction · planning target

Given an A-linear a:V→End_A(E) with pairwise commuting images, construct the unique A-algebra map α:S→End_A(E) satisfying α(ι(v))=a(v). For a=a_θ on finite locally free charts, this is the affine adapter of the existing integrable twisted Higgs symmetric action.

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. - `TwistedHiggsBundle.affineSymmetricAction.test_scalar` (computation): For E=Q=A and a(id_A)=id_E, the distinguished generator acts as identity, so the action is not nilpotent on a nonzero line.
- `TwistedHiggsBundle.affineSymmetricAction.test_rank_zero` (degenerate): On the zero module A^(Fin 0), every element of S acts by the zero endomorphism, including its unit.
- `TwistedHiggsBundle.affineSymmetricAction.test_noncommuting` (non-example): On ℚ² the actual endomorphisms E12 and E21 cannot both be images of degree-one generators under a symmetric-algebra action: their products differ on the first basis vector.
- `TwistedHiggsBundle.affineSymmetricAction.test_ambient_ideal` (non-example): On ℚ² set X=E12 and Y=E21. There exists the rank-one symmetric action α with ι(id_ℚ)↦X and I²⊆ker α because X²=0. But YX lies in the ambient left ideal span{X}, is nonzero, and (YX)²=YX. Thus forming the augmentation ideal in all End(ℚ²) instead of in S rejects this valid nilpotent action. This guards a potential implementation error, not a source erratum.

#### Symmetric extension and commuting contractions

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-symmetric-commuting` · lemma · planning target

An A-linear a:V→End_A(E) extends to an A-algebra map from S with generator values a iff a(v)a(w)=a(w)a(v) for every v,w. For a=a_θ and Q finite locally free, the existing exterior-coordinate theorem identifies this condition with θ∧θ=0.

**Hypotheses.** A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed. V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-symmetric-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-affine-symmetric-action), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/higgs-commuting`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-higgs-commuting).

**Proof route.**

1. For the forward implication apply α to ι(v)ι(w)=ι(w)ι(v) in the native commutative symmetric algebra.
2. For the reverse implication use affineSymmetricAction; no commutative ring instance is introduced on End(E).
3. Apply the existing H.0/higgs-commuting exterior basis argument locally; its i<j coefficients work in characteristic two without dividing by 2.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- An A-linear a:V→End_A(E) extends to an A-algebra map from S with generator values a iff a(v)a(w)=a(w)a(v) for every v,w. For a=a_θ and Q finite locally free, the existing exterior-coordinate theorem identifies this condition with θ∧θ=0.

#### Evaluation of a word of Higgs contractions

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/symmetric-action-word` · lemma · planning target

If α(ι(v))=a(v), then for every finite ordered list (v₁,…,v_N), α(ι(v₁)⋯ι(v_N))=a(v₁)⋯a(v_N). The empty word acts as id_E. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, so the rightmost listed contraction applies first.

**Hypotheses.** A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed. V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-symmetric-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-affine-symmetric-action).

**Proof route.**

1. The empty list uses α(1)=1 and the actual endomorphism unit.
2. Induct on list length using the algebra map multiplication law and the degree-one formula.
3. If a comes from an integrable field, commuting contractions permit reversal/reordering without changing this product; the ordered tensor-coordinate lemma below does not need that reordering.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- If α(ι(v))=a(v), then for every finite ordered list (v₁,…,v_N), α(ι(v₁)⋯ι(v_N))=a(v₁)⋯a(v_N). The empty word acts as id_E. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, so the rightmost listed contraction applies first.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-symmetric-action-morphism"></a>

#### Morphisms intertwine the symmetric action

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/symmetric-action-morphism` · lemma · planning target

For contraction maps a:V→End_A(E), b:V→End_A(F) and their generator-preserving actions α,β, an A-linear f:E→F satisfies f∘a(v)=b(v)∘f for every v iff f∘α(s)=β(s)∘f for every s∈S. For finite locally free Q these equalities identify Higgs-horizontal morphisms with intertwining the actual S-actions.

**Hypotheses.** A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed. V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative. F is another A-module. The action maps on both modules use the same coefficient dual V and the same symmetric algebra S.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-contractions`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-affine-contractions), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.0/affine-symmetric-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-0-affine-symmetric-action), `mathlib:SymmetricAlgebra.induction`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

**Proof route.**

1. An intertwiner of all s intertwines degree-one generators.
2. For the converse, use native symmetric-algebra induction on scalars, generators, sums and products. A-linearity of f handles scalars; composing the two induction equalities handles products.
3. On finite local bases, dual evaluation identifies the generator equalities with (f⊗id_Q)θ_E=θ_F f. Restriction and equality of sheaf maps glue; this is not a new module category carrier.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For contraction maps a:V→End_A(E), b:V→End_A(F) and their generator-preserving actions α,β, an A-linear f:E→F satisfies f∘a(v)=b(v)∘f for every v iff f∘α(s)=β(s)∘f for every s∈S. For finite locally free Q these equalities identify Higgs-horizontal morphisms with intertwining the actual S-actions.
