## H.8 — Real Noether–Lefschetz variation interfaces

The real weight-two branch uses the H.2 variation carrier and H.3 derivative geometry. Geometric complex-linear involution, coefficient conjugation and their combined conjugate-linear real action have different type behavior. Twisting by Z(1) changes the Galois sign. The moving-filtration derivative and the obstruction derivative of a transported flat class have opposite signs; this controls the normal-boundary factorization and Green surjectivity test.

The real Green criterion produces an open cone of transported algebraic classes after the real integral divisor theorem is imported. The Voisin kernel cone and genericity passage retain their analytic estimate and effective-weight-two hypotheses. Ordinary integral weak Lefschetz and affine Morse topology preserve torsion, while the VHS lattice has already quotiented it out. General involution/Morse foundations are requested at Geometric Topology Part II. Double covers, their particular vanishings and the period-index argument remain with RealSurfacePeriodIndex.

**Atlas landmarks.** [Real structure on a variation of Hodge structure](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action), [Noether–Lefschetz locus of a flat class](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus), [Kodaira–Spencer contraction](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-kodaira-spencer-contraction), [Griffiths derivative formula](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-griffiths-derivative), [Green's infinitesimal criterion over ℝ](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-green-open-cone), [Voisin's open cone in the push-forward kernel](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-kernel-cone).

### Declaration catalogue

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action"></a>

#### Compatible real action on a weight-two variation

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-action` · definition · planning target

On the imported finite-rank effective rational weight-two variation H over a smooth complex base with antiholomorphic involution c, a compatible real action is a rational local-system involution σ_b:H_Q,b→H_Q,c(b), with σ_c(b)σ_b=id, whose complex-linear extension exchanges H^(p,2-p)_b with H^(2-p,p)_c(b). Equivalently the semilinear composite τ_b=σ_C,b∘κ_b preserves Hodge types, where κ is coefficient conjugation. A flat G-stable chart identifies this data with an involutive real-linear σ on V=H_R,b and native fibre Hodge structures on C tensor_R V; it is only the action extension, not another VHS carrier.

**Hypotheses.** H is the common rational VHS of ShimuraData:D3, of weight 2 and effective in the sense of the native predicate HodgeStructureOn.IsEffective on each fibre. In the source the base is B(C) for a smooth algebraic variety B over R and c is its antiholomorphic involution; the definition uses only a complex manifold with an antiholomorphic involution. κ is the native conjugation; σ is geometric pullback, extended linearly in complex coefficients.

**Direct inputs.** `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.conj_piece`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.complexificationConjugation`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.IsEffective`.

**Proof route.**

1. Attach the rational involution to the existing local system and require its square and compatibility with transport.
2. Use native conj_piece to compare the type-exchange condition for σ_C with type preservation for σ_Cκ.
3. In a G-stable marking transport σ_b to one fixed real fibre; do not turn a choice of marking into global triviality.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A real structure acts between fibres b and c(b), not inside every non-real fibre.
- Separate σ_C from τ even at a fixed basepoint.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `RealActionOnChart.geometric` (data): The complexification of σ is a complex-linear map on the native tensor product; on z tensor v it is z tensor σ(v).
- `RealActionOnChart.combined` (data): The semilinear combined map sends z tensor v to conjugate(z) tensor σ(v).
- `RealActionOnChart.combined_involutive` (structure): Applying the combined map twice is the identity.
- `RealActionOnChart.combined_mem_piece` (compatibility): For x∈H_b^(p,2-p), τ(x)∈H_c(b)^(p,2-p); this is promoted as combined-type.
- `RealActionOnChart.ext` (extensionality): On the same supplied chart, equality of the real-linear geometric action determines equality of the compatible real-action structures.
- `RealActionOnChart.geometric_tmul` (simp): σ_C(z ⊗ v) = z ⊗ σ(v) for z∈C, v∈V.
- `RealActionOnChart.combined_tmul` (simp): τ(z ⊗ v) = conj(z) ⊗ σ(v) for z∈C, v∈V.
- `RealActionOnChart.geometric_piece` (projection): The defining compatibility: for every b and p, σ_C maps H_b^(p,2-p) onto H_c(b)^(2-p,p). It is an equality of native submodules, the image of piece p at b being piece 2−p at c(b).

**Unit tests.**

- `real_action_geometric_tensor` (computation): On a pure tensor, geometric action changes v and leaves the complex scalar z fixed.
- `real_action_combined_tensor` (compatibility): On a pure tensor, combined action changes v and conjugates z; on i tensor v it differs from geometric action by a minus sign.
- `real_action_zero` (degenerate): On the zero real vector space both geometric and combined action fix every vector.
- `real_action_combined_square` (characterisation): For every compatible chart action and vector x, τ(τ(x))=x.
- `real_action_identity_real_point` (non-example): If c is the identity and σ is the identity, compatibility forces H_b^(2,0)=0 (and so H_b^(0,2)=0) at every b: the image of piece 2 is piece 0, and the two meet in zero. So the identity is a real structure only on a variation of type (1,1); a definition asking σ_C to preserve types would accept it on every variation.

**Consumers.**

- `B18 Proposition1.1, pp.1050–1051`: Equivariance of the Hodge evaluation map allows passage to fixed real points.
- `B19 Proposition6.6, p.94; RealSurfacePeriodIndex consumer`: The class and vanishing summand carry geometric conjugation and the Tate sign.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.1, p.1050 (the action (1.1) and the Tate convention); equation (1.3), §1.4, p.1052 (its two factors). The source lets G act on the rational local system over the base involution, extends it to the complexified fibres by the action on the local system tensored with complex conjugation, and assumes that this antilinear action preserves the Hodge pieces; (1.3) writes it as coefficient conjugation followed by the complex-linear geometric map.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-combined-type"></a>

#### Type preservation of the combined real action

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/combined-type` · theorem · planning target

For a compatible real action and every b,p, τ_b maps H_b^(p,2-p) bijectively onto H_c(b)^(p,2-p). Coefficient conjugation and geometric complex-linear pullback each exchange the two indices; their composite preserves them.

**Hypotheses.** The real-action compatibility and involution laws of real-action.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action), `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.conj_piece`.

**Proof route.**

1. Apply the native coefficient-conjugation exchange to x.
2. Apply the geometric type exchange once more; 2-(2-p)=p.
3. Use the involution to obtain the reverse inclusion.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The theorem must preserve p; a theorem sending p to2-p describes one factor instead.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.1, p.1050; equation (1.3), §1.4, p.1052. Equation (1.3) factors the antilinear action as coefficient conjugation followed by the geometric map; each exchanges the Hodge pieces, so the composite preserves them.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-twisted-invariants"></a>

#### Tate-twisted invariant real fibre

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/twisted-invariants` · definition · planning target

For the untwisted real geometric involution σ on V, identify V(1)^G with the real submodule ker(σ+id) of V, using the generator 2πi of R(1). This is a coordinate identification of the native Tate twist with its sign action, not a new Tate-object definition. Write J_b for the intersection with the real (1,1) subspace at a real basepoint.

**Hypotheses.** The coefficient action on Z(1) is −1. B18 takes Z(1)=2πi·Z and B19 (§2.1, p.72) takes Z(1)=i·Z; both carry the sign action, so the identification with ker(σ+id) is the same. V carries an involutive real-linear geometric σ.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action), `mathlib:LinearMap.ker`, `mathlib:LinearMap.mem_ker`.

**Proof route.**

1. Represent the fixed-point equation for the product action as -σ(v)=v.
2. Use the native kernel submodule of σ+id, retaining its inherited module structure.
3. Intersect with the native fibre piece1 through 1 tensor v when a Hodge condition is needed.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Never identify twisted invariants with untwisted +1 eigenvectors.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `mem_twistedInvariants` (characterisation): v belongs to twistedInvariants σ iff σ(v)=-v; promoted as twist-sign.
- `twistedInvariants_id` (simp): For σ=id over R the twisted invariant submodule is zero.
- `twistedInvariants_neg_id` (simp): For σ=-id the twisted invariant submodule is all of V.
- `twistedInvariants_map` (functoriality): A real-linear map f with fσ=σ′f maps the twisted invariant submodule into the target twisted invariant submodule.
- `twistedInvariants_swap` (example): For the coordinate-swap involution on R² the twisted invariant vectors are exactly (a,-a).

**Unit tests.**

- `twisted_identity_line` (non-example): For V=R and σ=id, 1 is not twisted invariant.
- `twisted_negative_line` (computation): For V=R and σ=-id every vector is twisted invariant.
- `twisted_swap_plane` (characterisation): For swap(x,y)=(y,x), (x,y) is twisted invariant iff y=-x.
- `twisted_zero_space` (degenerate): On the zero real vector space twistedInvariants is top (and therefore also bottom).

**Consumers.**

- `B18 Proposition1.1, p.1050`: The initial Hodge class and target open cone lie in this twisted fixed space.
- `B19 Proposition6.6, p.94`: A real algebraic curve class is anti-invariant before Tate twisting.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.1, p.1050 (definition of Z(1) and of M(1), and the embedding of the twisted real (1,1) fibre). Z(1) is 2πi·Z with G acting by −1, M(1)=M⊗Z(1), and at a real point the twisted real (1,1) fibre is a G-stable real subspace of the complex fibre; its invariants are the classes used by Proposition 1.1.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-twist-sign"></a>

#### The real Tate sign equation

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/twist-sign` · lemma · planning target

Under the generator identification of V(1) with V, a vector is fixed by geometric conjugation tensored with the coefficient action on R(1) iff σ(v)=-v.

**Hypotheses.** Use the sign action on R(1), not coefficient conjugation on the untwisted real factor.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/twisted-invariants`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-twisted-invariants), `mathlib:LinearMap.mem_ker`.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand the tensor-product action on v tensor 2πi.
2. Cancel the fixed nonzero generator and rewrite -σ(v)=v.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Identity action gives no nonzero fixed twisted vector over R.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.1, p.1050. The sign action on Z(1) is part of the definition of the twisted fibre whose invariants enter Proposition 1.1.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-geometric-real-variation"></a>

#### Geometric real weight-two variation

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/geometric-real-variation` · theorem · planning target

If π:X→B is a smooth projective morphism of smooth algebraic varieties over R with surface fibres, the local system R²π_*Q on B(C), its Gauss–Manin bundle and Hodge filtration supplied by H.2 form an effective rational weight-two VHS with the compatible real action of real-action. Fibre H¹(Ω¹) identifies with H^(1,1), H²(O) with H^(0,2), and geometric conjugation sends the former Hodge type to its exchanged type at c(b). Torsion is removed only for the VHS lattice, H²(Z)/tors; ordinary integral topology below retains torsion.

**Hypotheses.** π is smooth and projective; X and B are smooth over R. Use the actual Betti/de Rham and coherent Hodge comparison, not an arbitrary chosen decomposition. The identification of H¹(Ω¹) with H^(1,1) and of H²(O) with H^(0,2) is the one H.2/geometric-pure constructs; ComplexComparisonPartII:C1 is cited for the coherent cohomology of the fibres only.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.2/geometric-pure`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-2-geometric-pure), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.2/gauss-manin`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-2-gauss-manin), `ComplexComparisonPartII:C5/repair-proper-de-rham-betti`, [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/combined-type`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-combined-type), `ComplexComparisonPartII:C1`.

**Proof route.**

1. Import the geometric pure variation and Gauss–Manin connection of H.2.
2. Pull back differential forms by the antiholomorphic geometric involution; it interchanges their holomorphic and antiholomorphic degrees.
3. Coefficient conjugation interchanges the degrees independently; conclude compatibility via combined-type.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A nonconstant smooth projective family need not have globally constant local system.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.4, pp.1051–1052: the paragraph containing equation (1.3), before Proposition 1.3. For a smooth projective morphism of smooth real varieties the source checks the hypothesis of §1.1: the action on R²π_*Q covers the base involution, coefficient conjugation exchanges the Hodge pieces, and so does the map induced by the antiholomorphic involution of the total space.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus"></a>

#### Transported Hodge-class locus

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-hodge-locus` · definition · planning target

In a flat marking on a connected simply connected analytic open Δ at b₀, and for λ∈H_R,b₀, define NL_Δ(λ)={b∈Δ | transported λ lies in H_b^(1,1)}. Equivalently for real λ, it lies in F¹_b. The real locus is NL_Δ(λ)∩B(R), and for the real theorem λ is in V(1)^G. A non-simply-connected base uses the class on a chosen local-system branch; no globally preferred transport is asserted.

**Hypotheses.** Δ is a flat trivializing chart; transport is the imported local-system identification. The fibre structures are effective of weight2 and λ is real; the F¹ equivalence requires reality.

**Direct inputs.** `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/geometric-real-variation`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-geometric-real-variation), `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.piece`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.mem_piece_iff`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.complexificationConjugation_toEquiv_tmul`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the native piece1 submodule for the marked fibre and take membership of 1 tensor λ.
2. For a real vector, coefficient conjugation fixes it, so membership in F¹ also implies membership in its conjugate.
3. Restrict to fixed basepoints only when asking for real deformations.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The zero class belongs at every point, so genericity is never defined by existence of some Hodge class alone.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `mem_transportedHodgeLocus` (characterisation): b∈NL(λ) iff 1 tensor λ∈(H_b).piece1.
- `transportedHodgeLocus_zero` (simp): NL(0)=Δ.
- `transportedHodgeLocus_constant` (example): For a constant Hodge family, NL(λ) is Δ when λ is of type(1,1) and is empty otherwise.
- `transportedHodgeLocus_changeMarking` (functoriality): A constant real-linear change of marking e transports Hodge subspaces and λ together, giving the same locus; promoted as transported-locus-gluing.
- `transportedHodgeLocus_F_one` (compatibility): For a real λ, membership in NL(λ) is equivalent to membership of its complexification in F¹.

**Unit tests.**

- `transported_zero` (degenerate): NL(0) is the whole supplied chart.
- `transported_constant_inside` (computation): A constant family and a class with 1 tensor λ∈H.piece1 give the whole chart.
- `transported_constant_outside` (non-example): For a constant family and a class outside H.piece1 the transported locus is empty.
- `transported_F_one` (compatibility): For an arbitrary weight-two native Hodge fibre, the real embedded vector has the same membership in piece1 and F¹.

**Consumers.**

- `B19 Theorem1.5, p.70 and Proposition6.6, p.94`: Transports a fixed cohomology class before asking whether a nearby fibre is of type(1,1).

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1, §1.2, pp.1050–1051. The conclusion of the proposition is about classes that, after the identification given by the trivialization, are of type (1,1) at a nearby real point.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Theorem1.5, §1, pp.70–71. Contractible neighbourhoods carry a constant marked real cohomology space in which the cone is stated.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-locus-gluing"></a>

#### Change of marking for transported class loci

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-locus-gluing` · theorem · planning target

On overlapping flat charts, let e be the constant transition equivalence. If it carries the marked Hodge piece1 at each point to the other marked piece1, then NL_H(λ)=NL_H′(eλ) on the overlap. Transport composition gives the cocycle compatibility; classes on a nontrivial monodromy loop are compared only after the corresponding monodromy action.

**Hypotheses.** Transition maps are constant local-system maps and the Hodge data and class are transformed together.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-hodge-locus`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus), `ShimuraData:D3/variation`.

**Proof route.**

1. Apply submodule-image membership through the injective complexification of e.
2. Use equality of transported marked fibre pieces pointwise.
3. Use the local-system cocycle law on triple overlaps.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Changing the class while holding the filtration fixed is not a change of marking.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.2, p.1050 (the trivialization over Δ and its uniqueness); proof of Proposition 1.1, p.1051. The identification of fibres is the one given by the trivialization of the local system, which is unique on a connected chart; this is what makes the marked statement independent of the chart.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-nl-obstruction-derivative"></a>

#### Derivative of the flat-class Hodge obstruction

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/nl-obstruction-derivative` · theorem · planning target

At a point where a flat real class λ belongs to F¹, its image in H_C/F¹ defines a local obstruction section with zero value. Under the fibre identification of that quotient with H^(0,2), its derivative is -θ_b(v)(λ), where θ is the H.3 period/Gauss–Manin symbol. The positive sign belongs to differentiation of the moving filtration; the negative sign belongs to the quotient of a fixed flat class.

**Hypotheses.** Use a flat trivialization and a differentiable local frame for F¹; evaluate at a zero of the obstruction.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-hodge-locus`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/period-symbol`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-period-symbol), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/derivative-connection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-derivative-connection).

**Proof route.**

1. Represent nearby F¹ as the graph of A(b):F¹_b₀→H_C/F¹_b₀.
2. The fixed class obstruction in this quotient frame is -A(b)λ.
3. Differentiate and import derivative-connection; a moving quotient frame adds no term at a zero.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A graph A(t)=tA₁ gives obstruction derivative -A₁λ.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/G68](#source-h-8-g68): Proposition (1.20) and Theorem (1.23), II.1(a), pp.814–815. The source computes the derivative of the moving filtration as cup product with the Kodaira–Spencer class. The opposite sign for the quotient class of a fixed flat vector is not in the source: it is the graph computation of this node.
- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1 proof, §1.2, p.1051. Surjectivity uses the variation derivative on the class, so this sign does not alter rank.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-kodaira-spencer-contraction"></a>

#### Kodaira–Spencer contraction by a Hodge class

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/kodaira-spencer-contraction` · definition · planning target

For a smooth projective complex surface family at b and λ∈H¹(X_b,Ω¹_X_b), define φ_λ:T_bB→H²(X_b,O_X_b) as v↦KS_b(v)∪λ, using the contraction T_X⊗Ω¹_X→O_X and the ordered cup product H¹(T_X)⊗H¹(Ω¹_X)→H²(O_X). The same definition applies in any fibre dimension where these groups are defined. Its local signature accepts actual supplied KS and cup linear maps; those arbitrary maps do not assert a geometric KS identity.

**Hypotheses.** Use the geometric deformation map of the actual family and coherent cohomology cup/contraction. The order is KS first, λ second, consistently with Griffiths.

**Direct inputs.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `mathlib:LinearMap.range_eq_top`.

**Proof route.**

1. Compose the deformation map with contraction cup product evaluated on λ.
2. Bundle the result as a complex-linear map in the tangent vector; the dependence on λ is complex-linear.
3. Keep the generic family definition separate from double-cover tangent-space presentations.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The target is H²(O), not H¹(Ω¹); no double-cover equation is part of the definition.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `contractedKS_apply` (simp): φ_λ(v)=cup(KS(v),λ).
- `contractedKS_zero_class` (simp): φ_0=0.
- `contractedKS_add_class` (structure): φ_(λ+μ)=φ_λ+φ_μ.
- `contractedKS_smul_class` (structure): φ_(aλ)=aφ_λ for a∈C.
- `contractedKS_precomp` (functoriality): Replacing KS by KS∘f replaces φ_λ by φ_λ∘f.

**Unit tests.**

- `contractedKS_scalar_fixture` (computation): For T=D=H11=H02=C, KS=id and cup(a,λ)=aλ, φ_3(2)=6.
- `contractedKS_zero_fixture` (degenerate): With KS=0 every φ_λ is zero.
- `contractedKS_precomp_fixture` (compatibility): Precomposing the scalar KS by multiplication by2 gives φ_3(1)=6.
- `contractedKS_zero_class_fixture` (non-example): For the scalar fixture φ_0 is not surjective onto the nonzero target C.

**Consumers.**

- `B18 Proposition2.1 pp.1053–1054`: The contraction is computed by normal/divisor connecting maps.
- `B19 Proposition6.6 p.94`: Its rank supplies the infinitesimal Green hypothesis on the vanishing summand.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): §5.2, equation (5.2), p.86. The map is the Kodaira–Spencer map of the family followed by the contracted cup product with λ coming from the pairing of the tangent sheaf with Ω¹.
- [H.8/G68](#source-h-8-g68): II.1(a), equation(1.19), Proposition(1.20), p.814. The ordered contraction cup product is the derivative map on Hodge components.
- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): §1.4, equation (1.4), p.1052. The same composite for an arbitrary smooth projective family of surfaces, as the form in which Griffiths' computation is used.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-griffiths-derivative"></a>

#### Griffiths derivative equals contraction

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/griffiths-derivative` · theorem · planning target

Let π:X→B be a smooth projective morphism of smooth complex algebraic varieties with surface fibres, and H the geometric weight-two variation of H.2/geometric-pure on R²π_*Q with its Gauss–Manin connection. Under the natural identifications H_b^(1,1)≅H¹(X_b,Ω¹) and H_b^(0,2)≅H²(X_b,O), θ_b(v)(λ)=φ_λ(v) for every v∈T_bB and λ∈H_b^(1,1), where θ_b is the H.3 period symbol at p=1 restricted to H_b^(1,1) and φ_λ(v)=KS_b(v)∪λ. The equality has positive sign in the H.3 convention; the separate flat-class obstruction has negative sign. No real structure enters: geometric-real-variation uses the formula after complexifying a real family.

**Hypotheses.** π is smooth projective over C with surface fibres, B smooth; use the natural coherent Hodge and de Rham/Betti comparisons. The identifications of H^(1,1) with H¹(Ω¹) and of H^(0,2) with H²(O) are those of H.2/geometric-pure: the graded pieces of the de Rham filtration are the Hodge cohomology groups. The engine behind them (degeneration and the cohomological Hodge decomposition) is gap G9 of that packet and is recorded here in G1; coherent analytic cohomology alone does not give it. The source proves the formula for any analytic family of compact Kähler manifolds and any degree; only weight two on surfaces is used here.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.2/geometric-pure`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-2-geometric-pure), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.2/gauss-manin`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-2-gauss-manin), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/kodaira-spencer-contraction`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-kodaira-spencer-contraction), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/period-symbol`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-period-symbol), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/derivative-connection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-derivative-connection), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `ComplexComparisonPartII:C5/repair-proper-de-rham-betti`.

**Proof route.**

1. Choose local family coordinates; derivatives of transition maps give the Čech KS cocycle.
2. Differentiate a representative (1,1)-form: the component lowering holomorphic degree is contraction with that cocycle.
3. The remaining components lie in F¹ and disappear in H_C/F¹; identify the remaining class by Griffiths Proposition(1.20).

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Comparison uses the actual geometric KS map; a declared linear map of the right type is insufficient.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/G68](#source-h-8-g68): II.1(a), equations(1.4)–(1.16), Proposition(1.20), Theorem(1.23), pp.810–815. The full local differential-form calculation identifies the period derivative with KS cup product.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition6.6 proof, p.94. This formula converts the contraction rank calculation into the variation derivative required by Green.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-normal-boundary-factorization"></a>

#### Normal-boundary factorization of divisor contraction

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/normal-boundary-factorization` · theorem · planning target

Let C⊂T⊂X be smooth projective complex varieties of dimensions 1, 2, 3, so that C is an effective Cartier divisor on T and T on X. Let ρ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→H¹(T,T_T) be the connecting map of 0→T_T→T_X|_T→N_T/X→0, and let λ∈H¹(T,Ω¹_T) be the class of C in Hodge cohomology, the first Chern class of O_T(C) defined through its Atiyah class. Then for every n∈H⁰(T,N_T/X), ρ(n)∪λ=δ_div(δ_norm(n|_C)) in H²(T,O_T), where δ_norm:H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C)→H¹(C,N_C/T) is the connecting map of 0→N_C/T→N_C/X→N_T/X|_C→0 and δ_div:H¹(C,N_C/T)→H²(T,O_T) is that of 0→O_T→O_T(C)→O_T(C)|_C→0, with O_T(C)|_C≅N_C/T. For a family of surfaces in X through T with base B, the Kodaira–Spencer map at T is ρ∘k, where k:T_bB→H⁰(T,N_T/X) classifies the first-order embedded deformations; hence φ_λ=δ_div∘δ_norm∘res_C∘k.

**Hypotheses.** C, T and X are smooth and projective over C, of dimensions 1, 2 and 3, with C⊂T⊂X. The Chern class and the boundary signs use the same generator of Z(1) and the cup ordering of kodaira-spencer-contraction. The identity is a statement about coherent cohomology. The source introduces λ as the image of the Betti class of C in H²(T(C),Z(1)); that this is the coherent Chern class is the comparison of first Chern classes under the de Rham–Betti isomorphism, needed only when the factorization is fed to the Griffiths formula, and is part of G1.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/kodaira-spencer-contraction`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-kodaira-spencer-contraction), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`.

**Proof route.**

1. Compute connecting maps by extension cocycles formed from differences of local splittings; a connecting map is cup product with the extension class.
2. Pull the divisor extension back along T_T→N_C/T (extended by zero from C): the resulting extension of T_T by O_T has class λ. The source proves this by twisting by O_T(−C) and identifying the result with the dual of Atiyah's extension, whose class is −λ; dualizing changes the sign once.
3. The map of normal sequences from (T_T, T_X|_T, N_T/X) to (N_C/T, N_C/X, N_T/X|_C) and the pull-back diagram give the compatibility of the two connecting maps, hence the identity.
4. For a family, compose with the characteristic map: the Kodaira–Spencer map of a family of hypersurfaces is the characteristic map followed by ρ (B19 quotes Sernesi, Proposition 3.2.9(i), for this).
5. Use the degree-one group H¹(C,N_C/T) in the middle; B19 (5.7) prints degree zero there (source issue E-H8-1).

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The middle cohomology group is H¹(C,N_C/T); replacing it by H⁰ is ill-typed.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition2.1, §2.1, pp.1053–1054. The full extension-class argument proves the equality of the normal-boundary composite and contraction.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition 5.4 proof, equations (5.7)–(5.9), p.88. The factorization is applied to the family of double covers, after describing its Kodaira–Spencer map through the characteristic map; (5.7) has the degree misprint recorded as E-H8-1.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-normal-vanishing-surjectivity"></a>

#### Generic vanishing criterion for divisor contraction

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/normal-vanishing-surjectivity` · theorem · planning target

In normal-boundary-factorization, if H¹(T,N_T/X(-C))=0, H¹(C,N_C/X)=0 and H²(T,O_T(C))=0, then φ_λ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→H²(T,O_T) is surjective. For a family with characteristic map k:T_bB→H⁰(T,N_T/X), the conclusion on T_bB additionally requires k to be surjective, or that the composite restriction from T_bB to H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C) be surjective.

**Hypotheses.** The three explicit vanishing hypotheses; a family parameter must supply the extra characteristic-map condition.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/normal-boundary-factorization`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-normal-boundary-factorization), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Proof route.**

1. The restriction exact sequence gives surjectivity to H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C).
2. The normal cohomology sequence gives surjectivity of δ_norm.
3. The divisor cohomology sequence gives surjectivity of δ_div; compose using normal-boundary-factorization.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Vanishing alone does not imply surjectivity for an arbitrary smaller parameter family.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Corollary2.2, §2.1, p.1054. The three stated vanishings force every map in the normal-boundary composite to be onto.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-positive-open-cone"></a>

#### Positive open cones of classes

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/positive-open-cone` · definition · planning target

A positive open cone Ω in a finite-dimensional real vector space V is a nonempty open subset closed under multiplication by every positive real scalar. It need not be convex or closed under addition, and zero is permitted. Its topology is that of V, or explicitly of a kernel/fixed subspace when that is the ambient space.

**Hypotheses.** V is a finite-dimensional normed real vector space; relative openness is stated in the actual target subspace.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:LinearMap.ker`, `mathlib:ConvexCone`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use a set with openness, nonemptiness and positive-scaling stability.
2. For positive a, stability for a and a⁻¹ gives aΩ=Ω.
3. A linear equivalence transports the set and all three properties.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The zero-dimensional target has the cone {0}; neither excluding zero nor demanding convexity is justified.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `PositiveOpenCone.smul_iff` (characterisation): For a>0, a•v∈Ω iff v∈Ω.
- `PositiveOpenCone.transport` (functoriality): A continuous real-linear equivalence transports a positive open cone to a positive open cone.
- `PositiveOpenCone.positiveRay` (example): The positive half-line (0,∞) is a positive open cone in R.
- `PositiveOpenCone.whole` (constructor): The whole real vector space is a positive open cone, including in dimension zero.
- `PositiveOpenCone.ofConvexCone` (compatibility): A Mathlib ConvexCone over R whose carrier is open and nonempty is a positive open cone with the same carrier. The converse fails: a positive open cone need not be closed under addition.

**Unit tests.**

- `cone_positive_ray` (computation): The positiveRay constructor supplies the cone conditions; its carrier contains 1 and excludes 0.
- `cone_zero_dimension` (degenerate): The entire zero-dimensional real vector space is a cone and contains zero.
- `cone_annulus_failure` (non-example): The nonempty open interval (1,2) is not a positive cone: positive scaling does not preserve it.
- `cone_scaling_inverse` (characterisation): For every positive a, membership of a•v in Ω is equivalent to membership of v.
- `cone_punctured_line` (non-example): The punctured line {x∈R : x≠0} is a positive open cone. It is not convex and not closed under addition (1+(−1)=0), so a definition through Mathlib's ConvexCone would reject it.

**Consumers.**

- `B19 Proposition1.2 proof p.71 and Proposition6.6 p.94`: A lattice-coset approximation is made in precisely the real subspace in which the cone is open.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1 and proof, §1.2, pp.1050–1051. Positive scaling of the fibrewise linear evaluation map expands its open image into a nonempty open cone.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Theorem1.5, pp.70–71. The cone is open in the pushforward kernel, not necessarily in all cohomology.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-green-evaluation-submersion"></a>

#### Green’s evaluation submersion criterion

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/green-evaluation-submersion` · theorem · planning target

Let H be a finite-rank effective real weight-two VHS on a complex manifold and choose a flat trivializing neighbourhood Δ of b. The smooth real bundle J of real (1,1)-classes has evaluation E:J→H_R,b by flat transport. If λ∈J_b and θ_λ:T_bB→H_b^(0,2) is onto as a complex-linear map, E is a submersion at (b,λ). The same statement holds for a rational subvariation, with its own Hodge pieces and target.

**Hypotheses.** The local system, differentiable Hodge bundle, flat marking and Griffiths symbol are those of the common variation supplier. Surjectivity is onto the (0,2) piece of the chosen variation, not onto the full ambient cohomology.

**Direct inputs.** `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/period-symbol`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-period-symbol), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/derivative-connection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-derivative-connection), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-hodge-locus`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus), `mathlib:HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorphOfComplemented`, `mathlib:HasStrictFDerivAt.mem_implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorphOfComplemented_target`, `mathlib:HasStrictFDerivAt.map_nhds_eq_of_surj`.

**Proof route.**

1. The fibre derivative contributes J_b.
2. The derivative normal to J_b is the real form of θ_λ and its conjugate; a real tangent vector of the complex base has arbitrary (1,0) component.
3. Complex surjectivity onto H^(0,2) therefore gives real surjectivity modulo J_b.
4. A submersion has open image near the point: Mathlib's map_nhds_eq_of_surj gives this directly in complete normed spaces; the implicit-function chart is the same statement with a straightening.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- A constant VHS with nonzero (0,2) piece cannot satisfy the hypothesis.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1 proof, §1.2, p.1051. Under the surjectivity hypothesis the evaluation from the real (1,1) bundle to the fixed real fibre is submersive at (b,λ); the source quotes Voisin's book for this.
- [H.8/V06](#source-h-8-v06): Lemma 2 and the proof of Proposition 1, §1, author PDF pp.4–5; Proposition 8 proof, §3, p.20. Lemma 2 states the equivalence between surjectivity of the contraction and submersivity of the evaluation on F¹; the proof of Proposition 1 passes to the real (1,1) bundle, and Proposition 8 repeats the argument for the push-forward kernel.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-fixed-linear-surjectivity"></a>

#### Surjectivity on real fixed tangent spaces

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/fixed-linear-surjectivity` · theorem · planning target

Let s:E→E and t:F→F be real-linear involutions, and L:E→F an equivariant surjective real-linear map. The restriction L:E^s→F^t is onto. This remains true after changing both actions by the Tate sign. It is the linear input to restricting an equivariant submersion to smooth fixed loci.

**Hypotheses.** Scalar field R, so2 is invertible. L∘s=t∘L; both actions are involutive.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:LinearMap.ker`, `mathlib:LinearMap.range_eq_top`.

**Proof route.**

1. For y fixed by t choose x with Lx=y.
2. The averaged vector (x+s(x))/2 is fixed by s and still maps to y.
3. Apply the argument to the actual tangent actions; nonlinear fixed-locus charts need the separate manifold supplier.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- In characteristic2 this averaging proof and general conclusion fail; the theorem is specifically real-linear.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1 proof, §1.2, p.1051. Tangent invariants of the two fixed loci retain surjectivity of the equivariant derivative.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-green-open-cone"></a>

#### Real Green open-cone theorem

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-green-open-cone` · theorem · planning target

Let H be an effective rational weight-two VHS on B(C), for a smooth algebraic variety B over R, with a compatible real action; let b∈B(R) and λ∈H_R,b^(1,1)(1)^G, and suppose θ_λ:T_bB(C)→H_b^(0,2) is surjective. Let Δ be any G-stable connected analytic neighbourhood of b in B(C) on which the local system is trivial and whose real locus Δ(R)=Δ∩B(R) is connected and contractible. Then there is a positive open cone Ω⊂H_R,b(1)^G such that every ν∈Ω, transported flatly over Δ, lies in H_R,b′^(1,1)(1)^G for some b′∈Δ(R): it is of type (1,1) there and is still twisted-invariant, because the marking of a G-stable chart is G-equivariant. Openness is relative to H_R,b(1)^G. Such neighbourhoods exist inside every neighbourhood of b, so Δ may be taken arbitrarily small; the cone depends on Δ.

**Hypotheses.** B is a smooth algebraic variety over R, so B(R) is the fixed locus of an antiholomorphic involution of the complex manifold B(C); the fixed Hodge bundle is a manifold whose tangent spaces are the fixed tangent spaces (the fixed-locus theorem of G3). λ has the Tate sign and is real of type (1,1); θ_λ is onto the complex (0,2) target. Δ is admissible in the sense of the statement; no smallness is needed beyond that.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-action`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-action), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/twist-sign`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-twist-sign), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/green-evaluation-submersion`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-green-evaluation-submersion), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/fixed-linear-surjectivity`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-fixed-linear-surjectivity), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/positive-open-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-positive-open-cone), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology#layer-1-manifold-library-buildout-general-dimension-general-structure-group`, `mathlib:HasStrictFDerivAt.map_nhds_eq_of_surj`.

**Proof route.**

1. Apply green-evaluation-submersion to the evaluation on the real (1,1) bundle over Δ; it is G-equivariant because the trivialization of a connected G-stable chart is unique.
2. Twist by Z(1) and pass to G-invariants: by the fixed-locus theorem and fixed-linear-surjectivity the restricted evaluation from the twisted-invariant (1,1) bundle over Δ(R) to H_R,b(1)^G is a submersion at (b,λ).
3. Its image therefore contains a neighbourhood of λ in H_R,b(1)^G (map_nhds_eq_of_surj in charts).
4. The image is stable under positive scaling because evaluation is fibrewise linear; the positive saturation of that neighbourhood is the cone, and it contains λ.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Neither existence of real basepoints nor complex Noether–Lefschetz density supplies the rank hypothesis.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.1 and its proof, §1.2, pp.1050–1051. For the neighbourhood chosen at the start of §1.2 the proposition gives an open cone in the twisted-invariant real fibre whose elements are, after the trivialization, twisted-invariant classes of type (1,1) at points of the real locus of the neighbourhood.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition6.6 proof, p.94. This criterion is invoked on the vanishing variation in the real-surface application.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-good-real-locus"></a>

#### Real infinitesimal Noether–Lefschetz locus

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/good-real-locus` · definition · planning target

For a compatible weight-two real variation, define Good_R(H)={b∈B(R) | there exists λ∈J_b=H_R,b^(1,1)(1)^G such that θ_λ:T_bB(C)→H_b^(0,2) is onto}. In a supplied chart this predicate uses an actual real submodule J_b and the real-linear class-to-symbol map J_b→Hom_C(T_bB,H_b^(0,2)); it is not existence of any Hodge class.

**Hypotheses.** Finite-dimensional Hodge pieces; the derivative family is the actual Griffiths symbol. Real-analyticity is required for the density theorem, not built into this set definition.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/twisted-invariants`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-twisted-invariants), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-hodge-locus`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-hodge-locus), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/period-symbol`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-period-symbol), `mathlib:LinearMap.range_eq_top`.

**Proof route.**

1. Quantify over the twisted real (1,1) subspace.
2. Express onto by the native linear-map range condition.
3. The zero target is handled without assuming a nonzero class exists.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- If H^(0,2)=0 the zero class witnesses goodness; if J=0 and the target is nonzero the point is bad.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Reusable API.**

- `mem_goodRealLocus` (characterisation): b is good iff some λ∈J_b gives a surjective symbol.
- `goodRealLocus_zero_target` (simp): When the target complex vector space is zero, every basepoint is good.
- `goodRealLocus_zero_symbol` (characterisation): For an identically zero class-to-symbol map, goodness is equivalent to the target being the zero space.
- `goodRealLocus_baseChange` (functoriality): Pointwise transport by source, target and class-space linear equivalences preserves goodness.

**Unit tests.**

- `good_scalar_symbol` (computation): For J=T=Q=C viewed with J as a real module and symbol(λ)(v)=λv, the one-point base is good, witnessed by 1.
- `good_zero_target` (degenerate): For Q=0 the zero class witnesses goodness at every point, even if J=0.
- `good_zero_class_space` (non-example): For J=0 and Q=C, the one-point base is bad.
- `good_constant_zero_symbol` (characterisation): For every nonzero Q the identically zero symbol gives the empty good locus.

**Consumers.**

- `B18 Propositions1.2–1.3 p.1052`: Provides the locus shown to be empty or dense in each real connected component.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.2, §1.3, p.1051. The real criterion locus asks whether some invariant twisted (1,1)-class has surjective derivative.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-good-locus-density"></a>

#### Componentwise density of the real criterion

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-good-locus-density` · theorem · planning target

For a finite-rank weight-two compatible real VHS over the complex points of a smooth real algebraic variety, Good_R(H) is open, and on each connected component K of B(R) it is either empty or open dense. In particular one good point in K implies density in that K. For a geometric smooth projective real family the condition is equivalently surjectivity of KS contraction on an invariant twisted (1,1)-class.

**Hypotheses.** The fixed Hodge bundle and derivative family have real-analytic local frames; fibre dimensions are locally constant. Connected components are those of the smooth real manifold B(R). Openness of the good locus is not in the source's statement; it follows from its proof, which shows that the complement is a closed real-analytic subset.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/good-real-locus`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-good-real-locus), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/griffiths-derivative`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-griffiths-derivative), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology#layer-1-manifold-library-buildout-general-dimension-general-structure-group`, `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero`.

**Proof route.**

1. In local frames expand maximal-rank minors as finite homogeneous polynomials in the class coordinates.
2. Badness at a basepoint means every coefficient of every such minor vanishes: this is a finite system of real-analytic equations, not an unproved arbitrary intersection assertion.
3. If badness contains a nonempty open set, the several-variable analytic identity principle propagates vanishing along the connected component.
4. Otherwise the closed bad set has empty interior; goodness is open dense. Use griffiths-derivative for the geometric formulation.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- No componentwise nonemptiness is asserted; the real criterion can fail everywhere.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Proposition 1.2 and its proof, §1.3, p.1051; Proposition 1.3, §1.4, p.1052. The real-analytic rank condition has the componentwise empty-or-dense alternative; the next proposition identifies the geometric criterion.
- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Remark1.5, p.1052. Complex density alone does not force the real criterion locus to be nonempty.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-orthogonal-constant-splitting"></a>

#### Constant and vanishing weight-two summands

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/orthogonal-constant-splitting` · theorem · planning target

Suppose an effective rational weight-two VHS has a flat rational symmetric bilinear pairing Q and a constant Hodge sub-local-system C with fixed Hodge filtration, such that Q restricted to C is nondegenerate and Q_C(H^(p,q),H^(r,s))=0 unless p+r=q+s=2. Then K=C^⊥ is a flat rational Hodge subvariation, H=C⊕K and the projector to C is flat and a Hodge morphism. A compatible real action preserving C and Q preserves K. In surface-cover applications Q is the full intersection pairing; it is not asserted to be a polarization of all H² without the Lefschetz sign correction.

**Hypotheses.** Q is flat and nondegenerate on C; C is a subvariation with constant Hodge filtration. Q is a Hodge pairing of total type(2,2), with the stated vanishing between unmatched Hodge types.

**Direct inputs.** `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, `ShimuraData:D3`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Hodge.RationalHodgeSubstructure.isCompl_WQ_orthogonal_WQ`, `mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_nondegenerate`.

**Proof route.**

1. Fibrewise, Mathlib's isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_nondegenerate gives H_b=C_b⊕C_b^⊥ from nondegeneracy of Q on C_b alone (Q symmetric, the fibre finite-dimensional). When Q is a polarization this agrees with the native Tau Ceti complement theorem, which is the polarized special case.
2. Flatness of Q and C makes the fibre orthogonal spaces locally constant under parallel transport.
3. Hodge-type orthogonality splits each piece and the filtration; nondegeneracy on C produces the direct sum.
4. Preservation of the two inputs by real action gives preservation of K.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For a degree-d surface map, p_*p^*=d on rational cohomology gives the normalized projector d⁻¹p^*p_* and identifies K with ker p_*.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition 6.6 proof, p.94. The weight-two variation decomposes as the constant cohomology of the base surface and its cup-product orthogonal vanishing subvariation.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-constant-symbol-zero"></a>

#### No derivative into a constant Hodge summand

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/constant-symbol-zero` · theorem · planning target

For the flat Hodge splitting H=C⊕K with C having constant Hodge filtration, the period symbol respects the splitting and its C-part vanishes: θ_b(v) is zero on C_b^(1,1) and maps K_b^(1,1) into K_b^(0,2). Hence, writing λ=λ_C+λ_K for λ∈H_b^(1,1), θ_λ=θ_(λ_K), and θ_λ(T_bB) lies in K_b^(0,2).

**Hypotheses.** Use the flat Hodge projector of orthogonal-constant-splitting.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/orthogonal-constant-splitting`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-orthogonal-constant-splitting), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/period-symbol`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-period-symbol), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.3/derivative-connection`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-3-derivative-connection).

**Proof route.**

1. A parallel C-section remains in the same filtration step, so its Gauss–Manin symbol is zero.
2. Naturality of the symbol under the flat projector kills the C-projection of θ_λ.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- Constancy of the underlying local system alone is insufficient; the Hodge filtration of C must also be constant.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition6.6 proof, p.94. The derivative has image in the vanishing part, because the other summand is constant.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-vanishing-rank-criterion"></a>

#### Codimension criterion on the vanishing summand

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/vanishing-rank-criterion` · theorem · planning target

Let H_b^(0,2)=C_b^(0,2)⊕K_b^(0,2), and f:T_bB→H_b^(0,2) have image in K_b^(0,2). If codim_(H^(0,2))(im f)≤dim_C C_b^(0,2), then f, with codomain restricted to K_b^(0,2), is surjective. The inequality is equivalent to equality because the image containment gives the reverse bound.

**Hypotheses.** Finite-dimensional complex vector spaces; the actual image-containment and direct-sum identification are supplied.

**Direct inputs.** `mathlib:LinearMap.range_eq_top`, `mathlib:Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_le`.

**Proof route.**

1. Write dim H=dim C+dim K and codim(im f)=dim C+dim K-dim(im f).
2. The stated inequality gives dim(im f)≥dim K; containment gives the reverse inequality.
3. Equal dimensions and containment force equality of subspaces.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- No codimension estimate for double covers is proved here; that is consumer data.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition6.6 proof, p.94. The consumer’s codimension estimate at most h²(O_S) implies onto the vanishing(0,2)-piece.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-vanishing-real-green"></a>

#### Real Green criterion for the vanishing variation

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/vanishing-real-green` · application · planning target

Under orthogonal-constant-splitting with a compatible real action preserving C and Q, let b be real and let λ∈H_R,b^(1,1)(1)^G be a twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of the ambient variation; in the source it is the class of a real curve, which does not lie in K. If the cokernel of its geometric contraction φ_λ:T_bB(C)→H_b^(0,2) has dimension at most dim_C C_b^(0,2), then for every admissible neighbourhood Δ of b as in real-green-open-cone, now trivializing K, there is a positive open cone in K_R,b(1)^G whose classes, transported over Δ, are twisted-invariant classes of K of type (1,1) at points of Δ(R). The cone is open in the vanishing twisted-invariant subspace.

**Hypotheses.** The constant summand has constant Hodge filtration, and the splitting is compatible with the real action. λ is any twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of H at b; the theorem is applied to its K-component λ_K, which is again real, of type (1,1) and twisted-invariant because the Hodge projector is rational, flat and commutes with the real action. All geometric comparison suppliers of griffiths-derivative are supplied.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/orthogonal-constant-splitting`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-orthogonal-constant-splitting), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/griffiths-derivative`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-griffiths-derivative), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/constant-symbol-zero`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-constant-symbol-zero), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/vanishing-rank-criterion`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-vanishing-rank-criterion), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-green-open-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-green-open-cone).

**Proof route.**

1. Compare the contraction with the period symbol by griffiths-derivative.
2. By constant-symbol-zero, θ_λ=θ_(λ_K) and its image lies in K_b^(0,2); by vanishing-rank-criterion it is onto K_b^(0,2).
3. Apply real-green-open-cone to the subvariation K and the class λ_K.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The application does not replace the ambient rank estimate by a hypothesis of surjectivity onto all H²(O).

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition 6.6 proof, p.94. The class of the curve is a twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of the whole variation; its derivative has cokernel of dimension at most h²(O_S) and image in the vanishing part, hence is onto the vanishing (0,2)-piece, and the real criterion is then applied to the vanishing variation.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-full-lattice-coset-cone"></a>

#### Full lattice cosets meet positive open cones

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/full-lattice-coset-cone` · theorem · planning target

Let V be a finite-dimensional normed real space, b a finite real basis, Λ=span_Z(range b), n a positive integer, a∈V and Ω a positive open cone in V. Then (a+nΛ)∩Ω is nonempty. Thus the result applies to every full-rank finite-index sublattice and every coset in its real span; it does not apply to a lower-rank lattice in a larger ambient space.

**Hypotheses.** n>0; openness and nonemptiness hold in the same full real span as the lattice. No rationality of the cone or of a is needed.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/positive-open-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-positive-open-cone), `mathlib:ZSpan.floor`, `mathlib:ZSpan.norm_fract_le`.

**Proof route.**

1. Choose v∈Ω and a ball of radius ε>0 around v contained in Ω.
2. For large t>0 choose z=floor_b((t v-a)/n); native norm_fract_le bounds ||a+nz-tv|| by n times the sum of basis norms.
3. After dividing by t the error tends to zero, so (a+nz)/t belongs to the chosen ball.
4. Positive-scaling stability gives a+nz∈Ω; dimension zero is automatic.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The positive real ray meets every congruence class a+nZ for n>0.
- For Λ=Z×{0} in R², a cone disjoint from that axis demonstrates why full rank matters.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition1.2 proof, p.71; Proposition6.6 proof, p.94. A prescribed coset of a full lattice meets the open cone; the real proof uses the same elementary approximation.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-infinitesimal-kernel"></a>

#### Voisin’s high-degree kernel rank theorem

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-infinitesimal-kernel` · theorem · planning target

Let X be a smooth projective complex threefold with a morphism p:X→S to a smooth projective surface, whose generic fibre is a smooth rational curve. Choose an ample line bundle H with H²·K_X<0; replacing H by a sufficiently high positive power provides the very-ampleness and positive-twist cohomology hypotheses used in the proof. For all sufficiently large m and a general smooth T∈|mH|, there is λ∈ker[p_*:H¹(T,Ω¹_T)→H¹(S,Ω¹_S)] for which φ_λ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→ker[p_*:H²(T,O_T)→H²(S,O_S)] is surjective.

**Hypotheses.** p is a morphism with rational generic fibre; X,S smooth projective over C. The negative canonical intersection hypothesis and all sufficiently-large-degree bounds in Voisin’s proof are retained.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/kodaira-spencer-contraction`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-kodaira-spencer-contraction), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`, `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1`, `ComplexComparisonPartII:C1`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the bilinear cup pairing and Serre duality to reduce generic surjectivity to absence of oversized components of its projective base locus (Voisin Lemma6).
2. Degenerate to determinantal nodal surfaces; the limiting pairing includes products of evaluations at the nodes (Lemma7). Barth’s node count, Grassmannian Koszul/Bott vanishing and uniform position give the O(m²) projection/rank bound.
3. The generic low-rank loci have dimension bounded independently of m (Proposition5, projection to P³ and Fermat Jacobian-ring count). Green’s linear-series growth estimate then rules out bounded nonzero ranks (Propositions6–7).
4. In the kernel setting, the natural pushforward identifies H³(X,Ω¹_X) with H²(S,O_S), so the surface pushforward kernel equals the Gysin kernel. Residues span this kernel on H²(O_T); the annihilator under Serre duality is p^*H⁰(S,K_S), disjoint from its kernel by the pull-push degree identity. This is the modification in Proposition9.
5. These general proof suppliers have explicit requests and gaps; no unresolved cited estimate is described as a native library theorem.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- When H²(O_S) is nonzero, the target remains the kernel; no full-target surjectivity is claimed.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/V06](#source-h-8-v06): Proposition9, §3 author PDF p.21; full support: Lemmas6–10, Propositions3–7, §2 pp.8–18 and Appendix pp.22–23. The high-degree kernel contraction is onto, using the listed general nodal, rank, linear-series and residue arguments.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Theorem1.5 and explanatory paragraph, pp.70–71. The required kernel infinitesimal criterion is the Voisin result that produces the complex cone.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-kernel-cone"></a>

#### Voisin’s pushforward-kernel open cone

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-kernel-cone` · theorem · planning target

Under voisin-infinitesimal-kernel, for all sufficiently large m there is a nonempty Zariski open V in the smooth-divisor parameter space |mH| such that for every b∈V(C) and every connected contractible neighbourhood Δ of b in V(C), some positive open cone Ω⊂ker[p_*:H²(T_b,R)→H²(S,R)] consists of classes which become type(1,1) on a fibre over Δ. This is a complex deformation theorem: the points realizing the classes are in Δ(C), and no real-locus conclusion is included.

**Hypotheses.** The pushforward is a flat Hodge map in the universal divisor family; its kernel is a common-carrier weight-two subvariation. Voisin’s general high-degree hypothesis and the kernel rank theorem are supplied.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-infinitesimal-kernel`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-infinitesimal-kernel), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/green-evaluation-submersion`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-green-evaluation-submersion), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/positive-open-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-positive-open-cone), `ShimuraData:D3/variation`, `ShimuraData:D3`, `ComplexComparisonPartII:C5/repair-proper-de-rham-betti`, [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/griffiths-derivative`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-griffiths-derivative).

**Proof route.**

1. Flat pushforward defines the kernel local system, with constant rank and induced Hodge filtration.
2. Turn the contraction of voisin-infinitesimal-kernel into the period symbol by griffiths-derivative. Push-forward is a morphism of variations, so the symbol of H restricts to K=ker p_*, and surjectivity of φ_λ onto the kernel in H²(O) is surjectivity of θ_λ onto K^(0,2).
3. The infinitesimal theorem holds on a nonempty open rank locus; existence of some λ is an algebraic open condition by maximal minors in local frames.
4. The full-rank condition is a nonempty polynomial open set in the complex (1,1) kernel. Its coefficient-conjugation fixed real form is Zariski dense, so a real (1,1) class can be chosen with the same surjectivity.
5. Apply Green’s evaluation submersion argument within this kernel and saturate the image by positive scaling.
6. Choose a sufficiently small analytic chart inside each specified contractible neighbourhood, and use its flat marking. The resulting cone also works in the larger neighbourhood.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The ambient is ker p_*; it is neither all H² nor an unspecified quotient by pullbacks.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/V06](#source-h-8-v06): Proposition8 proof, §3 author PDF p.20, and Proposition9 p.21. The kernel Hodge evaluation is a submersion and hence has cone image.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Theorem1.5 and discussion, pp.70–71. The theorem is expressed uniformly on a nonempty Zariski open set of the smooth-divisor family.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-product-surface"></a>

#### The product-threefold kernel-cone interface

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-product-surface` · application · planning target

Let S be a connected smooth projective complex surface and A a very ample line bundle with A²>K_S·A. Put X=P¹×S, p=pr_S and H=pr_1^*O(1)⊗pr_S^*A. For all sufficiently large positive m, the smooth members T of |mH| have a nonempty Zariski open parameter set V satisfying the kernel-cone conclusion of voisin-kernel-cone for p:T→S. The integer m is a geometric degree threshold, unrelated here to a Brauer period.

**Hypotheses.** S connected, smooth and projective; A very ample; strict numerical inequality A²>K_S·A. The conclusion is a complex nearby-fibre statement.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-kernel-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-kernel-cone), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`.

**Proof route.**

1. The generic fibre of X→S is P¹.
2. Compute H²·K_X=2(K_S·A-A²)<0 using the product intersection relations.
3. Apply the general Voisin kernel theorem, retaining a sufficiently large m.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The inequality is strict; A²=K_S·A does not meet the hypothesis.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Theorem1.5, §1, p.70; proof explanation pp.70–71. The product surface interface and numerical positivity are exactly the instance required by the complex period-index argument.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-affine-cw-bound"></a>

#### Andreotti–Frankel affine CW bound

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-cw-bound` · theorem · planning target

Every smooth complex affine variety of complex dimension d has the homotopy type of a CW complex of real dimension at most d. In particular a smooth affine complex surface has CW dimension at most2. The statement is ordinary topology; a finite étale cover is another affine variety and must have the theorem applied to it separately.

**Hypotheses.** Smooth affine of pure complex dimension d; singular affine varieties require a different theorem.

**Direct inputs.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology#layer-1-manifold-library-buildout-general-dimension-general-structure-group`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-4-cw-pairs-cellular-homology-and-cofibrations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lane-m-morse-homology-stage-0`, `tauceti:TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint`, `tauceti:TauCeti.morseIndex`, `tauceti:TauCeti.morseIndex_comp`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ae_hasNondegenerateCriticalPointsOn_sub_inner`.

**Proof route.**

1. Embed the affine variety as a closed complex submanifold M of C^N.
2. For almost every point p the squared distance from p, restricted to M, has only nondegenerate critical points. In a chart of M formed by 2d of the real ambient coordinates it is a fixed function minus an inner-product term in the chart coordinates, so Tau Ceti's genericity theorem for inner-product perturbations applies chart by chart; countably many charts give almost every p. The function is proper and bounded below because M is closed.
3. At a critical point the native Morse index, read in a chart through its invariance under changes of coordinates, is at most d: in a normal direction the second fundamental form of a complex submanifold is the real part of a holomorphic quadratic form, whose eigenvalues occur in opposite pairs, so at most d of the 2d Hessian eigenvalues are negative (Milnor, §7, Assertions 1 and 2).
4. The handle theorem for a nondegenerate function with compact sublevel sets (Milnor, Theorem 3.5) gives a CW model with one cell of dimension the index for each critical point. That theorem is stated by no roadmap and is gap G3. Nondegenerate critical points, the Morse index and generic Morse perturbations are already in Tau Ceti at the pin, on normed spaces; their manifold-level form belongs to the Morse homology lane of the upstream Heegaard Floer roadmap, for which they were built.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- The bound is d, not the real manifold dimension2d; smoothness and affineness are essential.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/M63](#source-h-8-m63): §7 Theorem7.2 and full proof, pp.39–41. The closed complex-submanifold case has a CW model of dimension at most its complex dimension.
- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition 3.2 proof, §3.3, p.78, citing Andreotti–Frankel, Theorem 1. The surface proof uses the affine CW dimension bound to kill high-degree ordinary integral cohomology.
- [H.8/M63](#source-h-8-m63): §3, Theorem 3.5, p.20. A manifold with a nondegenerate function all of whose sublevel sets are compact has the homotopy type of a CW complex with one cell of dimension equal to the index for each critical point; this is the handle-to-CW input.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-affine-integral-vanishing"></a>

#### High-degree integral cohomology of affine surfaces

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-integral-vanishing` · theorem · planning target

For a smooth complex affine surface U, H^i(U(C),Z)=0 for every i≥3. The same conclusion holds for any smooth finite étale cover U′, since it is affine of the same dimension. No vanishing of sign local-system or equivariant cohomology is inferred merely by replacing the coefficient object.

**Hypotheses.** Ordinary singular cohomology with all integral torsion retained. The finite étale cover is smooth and affine; local-system conclusions require additional supplied sequences.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-cw-bound`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-affine-cw-bound), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-4-cw-pairs-cellular-homology-and-cofibrations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-6-cohomology-products-and-manifold-duality`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use affine-cw-bound in dimension2.
2. The integral cellular cochain complex has no terms above degree2, so its higher cohomology vanishes.
3. Apply the same reasoning independently to the cover.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- No argument passes through rational cohomology; torsion in low degrees is allowed.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition 3.2 proof, §3.3, p.78. Ordinary integral vanishing is proved first for the affine surface and its étale double cover; the sign-coefficient sequence is an additional step.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h3"></a>

#### Ordinary integral weak Lefschetz Gysin isomorphism

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h3` · theorem · planning target

For a smooth projective complex threefold X and a smooth ample Cartier surface i:T↪X, the ordinary integral Gysin map i_*:H³(T(C),Z)→H⁵(X(C),Z) is an isomorphism, including torsion.

**Hypotheses.** Smooth projective X of complex dimension3; T smooth and ample. Use complex orientations and integral Poincaré duality.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-cw-bound`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-affine-cw-bound), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-6-cohomology-products-and-manifold-duality`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`.

**Proof route.**

1. The complement X\T is affine: a positive multiple of the ample divisor gives a projective embedding whose hyperplane support is T.
2. Apply the dimension3 affine CW bound and relative integral duality to obtain H_j(X,T;Z)=0 for j≤2.
3. The pair homology sequence gives H₁(T,Z)≅H₁(X,Z).
4. Poincaré duality identifies these homology groups with H³(T,Z), H⁵(X,Z), and identifies inclusion with Gysin.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- An equivariant or étale weak Lefschetz theorem cannot replace this ordinary integral statement.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Lemma1.3 proof, §1, p.70. The proof explicitly uses the isomorphism H³(T,Z)→H⁵(X,Z).
- [H.8/M63](#source-h-8-m63): §7 Corollary7.3 and proof, p.41. Integral weak Lefschetz follows from the affine CW bound and relative duality.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h2"></a>

#### Ordinary integral weak Lefschetz Gysin surjectivity

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h2` · theorem · planning target

Under ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h3, the ordinary integral Gysin map i_*:H²(T(C),Z)→H⁴(X(C),Z) is surjective, including torsion. No injectivity is asserted.

**Hypotheses.** The same smooth ample complex3fold/surface hypotheses and integral orientation conventions.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-cw-bound`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-affine-cw-bound), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-6-cohomology-products-and-manifold-duality`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5`.

**Proof route.**

1. The same relative homology vanishing yields H₂(T,Z)→H₂(X,Z) onto.
2. Integral Poincaré duality identifies it with the Gysin map in cohomological degrees2 and4.
3. Keep the middle-degree kernel, which is typically the nontrivial vanishing cohomology.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- For X=P³ and T a smooth quartic K3, the source rank22 versus target rank1 makes an isomorphism assertion false.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Lemma1.4 proof, §1, p.70. The integral Gysin surjection is used to correct a class before applying the cone theorem.
- [H.8/M63](#source-h-8-m63): §7 Corollary7.3, p.41. The boundary-degree inclusion on integral homology is surjective.

<a id="node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-divisor-export"></a>

#### Transported integral Hodge classes and divisor conversion

`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-divisor-export` · application · planning target

On a smooth projective complex surface family, an integral class whose realification lies in a Green/Voisin cone becomes type(1,1) on a nearby fibre; the existing integral Lefschetz(1,1) supplier then gives a line bundle on that fibre with that first Chern class. For a real family, the H.8 cone supplies a nearby real point and a twisted invariant real Hodge class. To infer a real line bundle, the consumer must also provide an integral equivariant lift in H²_G(T(C),Z(1)) and use the real Lefschetz(1,1) extension of the cycle supplier. Untwisted invariance, rational classes, or invariant ordinary integral cohomology alone are insufficient replacements.

**Hypotheses.** For complex divisor conversion the class is integral, including any torsion; its type is tested after complexification. For real divisor conversion require the actual equivariant integral lift and the real cycle-class theorem. Transport of a chosen equivariant/relative lift, and finite-index lattice image, are consumer/topology inputs.

**Direct inputs.** [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-locus-gluing`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-locus-gluing), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/real-green-open-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-real-green-open-cone), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-kernel-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-kernel-cone), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/full-lattice-coset-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-full-lattice-coset-cone), `MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.7/tate-and-hodge-known-cases`, `MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.7`.

**Proof route.**

1. Use transported-locus-gluing to compare class transport with the marked cone conclusion.
2. Apply the already planned complex integral Lefschetz(1,1) known case in MC.7, rather than reproducing the exponential-sequence proof.
3. In the real case use the requested real cycle-class refinement only after receiving the equivariant lift.
4. Return the nearby fibre and divisor class; the double-cover, relative-pair/Kummer and period-index argument belongs to RealSurfacePeriodIndex.

**Acceptance boundary.**

- No claim that every G-invariant ordinary integral Hodge class descends to a real line bundle.

**Placement.** module: `TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/RealNoetherLefschetz`; namespace: `TauCeti.Hodge.RealNL`.

**Sources.**

- [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Proposition1.2 proof, p.71; Proposition6.6 proof, pp.94–95. The cone theorem is followed by integral(1,1) divisor conversion; the real argument uses the equivariant integral lift and real Lefschetz(1,1).
- [H.8/B18](#source-h-8-b18): Remark1.4, p.1052. The twisted real invariance convention is the convention satisfied by real divisor classes.
- [H.8/BW20](#source-h-8-bw20): §2.3.1, Proposition 2.8 (arXiv numbering). For a smooth proper variety over R, every class in the equivariant group H²_G(X(C),Z(1)) whose image in ordinary cohomology is a Hodge class is the equivariant cycle class of a line bundle on X; in degree two there is no further topological condition.

Missing exact reusable suppliers are: Barth’s node count for generic symmetric determinantal surfaces; the incidence Grass(2,m) Koszul/Bott vanishings of Proposition3 and Appendix Lemmas8,13; Harris uniform position for those node sets; Green/Macaulay low-codimension multiplication (Proposition7); Griffiths Jacobian-ring/residue identifications and the kernel residue exactness of Proposition9. Existing SF/moduli/comparison directions are requested for their portions, but no exact atlas node for the combinatorial linear-series and nodal uniform-position inputs was located. This is source-proof closure work, not an omission of the mandatory kernel-cone target. The push-forward identification H³(X,Ω¹_X)≅H²(S,O_S) for a morphism with rational generic fibre, used in the first step of Proposition 9, is in the same position.

Affected targets: [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-infinitesimal-kernel`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-infinitesimal-kernel), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-kernel-cone`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-kernel-cone), [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-product-surface`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-voisin-product-surface).

**H.8/G5: Real integral divisor-class refinement.** MC.7/tate-and-hodge-known-cases supplies the complex integral (1,1) theorem. The real refinement is Benoist–Wittenberg, Proposition 2.8 (after Krasnov): on a smooth proper variety over R, an equivariant class in H²_G(X(C),Z(1)) with Hodge image is the class of a line bundle. It is catalogued (PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20/divisor-real-lefschetz, PAPER-BENOIST-19/90) and routed to MC.7, but no node of MC.7 states it yet. Its statement was read; its proof is by references that were not obtained. H.8 exports the twisted real Hodge class; real line-bundle conversion requires the requested register entry and an actual consumer-supplied equivariant integral lift.

Affected targets: [`HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/transported-divisor-export`](#node-hodgestructurespartii-h-8-transported-divisor-export).

### Source corrections — H.8

**HodgeStructuresPartII/E-H8-1.** [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Published version, Proposition5.4 proof, equation(5.7), p.88.

The group is H¹(C,N_C/T), followed by the divisor connecting map to H²(T,O_T).

The normal short exact sequence gives a boundary H⁰(N_T/X|C)→H¹(N_C/T); B18 Proposition2.1 uses precisely that degree.

Review status: confirmed. Already confirmed as PAPER-BENOIST-19/E12 in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-BENOIST-19.json, reviewed by REV-ERRATA-PAPER-BENOIST-19.

**HodgeStructuresPartII/E-H8-2.** [H.8/V06](#source-h-8-v06): Author preprint §2, Corollary4(ii), author PDF p.13.

The second alternative bounds dim pr₂(Z′); the first bounds dim pr₁(Z′).

The two components in(2.7) bound different projection directions; the proof’s final sentence and Corollary5(ii) explicitly use the second direction. The page image was checked against the extracted text.

Review status: confirmed. Scoped to the author preprint; no claim that the version of record contains this misprint.

**HodgeStructuresPartII/E-H8-3.** [H.8/B19](#source-h-8-b19): Published version, Proposition 6.6 proof, p.94 (the application of the real Green criterion to the vanishing variation).

Apply the criterion to the vanishing component λ_van of λ, the image of λ under the Hodge projector of the splitting, and note that the derivative of λ_van equals that of λ because the other component is a flat class of the constant summand that stays of type (1,1).

The proposition quoted requires a twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of the variation it is applied to. The class of C is not in the vanishing part: its push-forward to S is the class of the image curve, a nonzero multiple of the class of an ample line bundle. Its vanishing component is again real, of type (1,1) and twisted-invariant, since the projector is rational, flat and G-equivariant, and it has the same derivative.

Review status: confirmed. new

## Assembly boundary and continuation

The [assembly handoff](../handoff/ASM-HodgeStructuresPartII.md) collects every supplier request and restructure proposal, the refined H.7→H.6 dependency map, the remaining coarse internal references and the Lean verification limit. This assembly preserves the accepted review verdicts. Closing a mathematical gap requires work at its stated owner and independent review; historical prototype receipts and omission inventories do not close it.
